Human reason is even more incapable of searching out the "cry" that came up before Him. Therefore, human reason thinks that God dwells only on high above the stars, alone in a heaven, and looks down here below just as the luster of the sun shines from its body upon the Earth. Reason reaches that far, but it knows nothing further of what God is or where He dwells. It does not know that He is every essence <note>original: "Essence"</note>, and dwells through every essence or being, and occupies no specific location; He also needs no place or space for His habitation. Yet He is present through all things and gives of Himself in an active and powerful way <note>original: "Energeticall"</note> <margin>Active or effective.</margin> to every essence, just as the powerful influence of the sun affects fruit. But He works with the creature and its life not from the outside in, but from the inside out, for His own manifestation. This material world <note>original: "nature"</note> <margin>Material substance.</margin> and every creature are His manifestation. If reason understood this correctly, it would have no further doubt <note>original: "Question"</note> <margin>Reason.</margin>, but would be undoubtedly satisfied within itself regarding what God is.

4. Now, understand the sum of all this briefly: God dwells in Himself, according to both Love and Anger. Each property sees only into itself and is not visible <note>original: "manifest"</note> in the other property. You have an analogy <note>original: "similitude"</note> of this in day and night—specifically, in light and darkness. The light dwells in the darkness and does not see it; likewise, the darkness does not see the light. Just as light dwells in its great gentleness within the fire, yet does not take the pain or source of the fire into itself, it remains only good without feeling the life of the fire. Yet it arises through the consuming of the fire, which is the "dying" of the substance <note>original: "Essence"</note>. Understand the being of God in this same way.

This is called the *Great Disturbance* <note>original: *Turba magna*</note> <margin>* Or, a darting flash.</margin>, which is a disturbance in the soul of the outward world within the spirit of nature. This causes the outward nature to ignite and kindle itself; and the * three first properties <margin>* The primary ternary of nature.</margin> fix themselves into a *substance*: specifically into sulfur, salt, and a poisonous mercurial water. The flash of the fire kindled and impressed itself into these; and once kindled, it rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah, and upon the plain of the country, destroying everything. This is what is meant when it says, *The Lord rained sulfur and fire from the Lord out of Heaven.*

27. This does not mean that this matter of the sulfur and fire came from the inner heaven. Instead, the wrath came forth from the inward realm into the outward realm <note>original: "Principle"</note>, so that the outward world, by the power of the inward, impressed and ignited itself from the properties of the inward. This is a real symbol <note>original: "Type"</note> of the inward dark world. If that same nature moves itself, then it exists in a spiritual property that God calls His wrath, anger, and a consuming fire. For if this inward spiritual dark world were to move itself, the outward world and its four elements would immediately be swallowed up by this same spiritual fire. This is what will happen at the *End of Days.*

28. And here we have a symbolic figure of this in *Lot’s wife, who was turned into a pillar of salt.* The "three first" properties had moved within her. Because she looked back into the *Disturbance* <note>original: *Turba*</note>, she was seized by the *spirit of salt* as it took hold. This signifies that she was * dominated by that very property—namely, she was greedy <note>original: "Covetous"</note> in her desire. <margin>* Or, that property was most predominant in her.</margin> Because of this, she was caught and held during the testing <note>original: "probation"</note> of the Angel.

29. Even though the Angel had protected her from the wrath of the fire, she was still caught in the natural wrath of her own specific character. The *Great Disturbance* <note>original: *Turba magna*</note> laid hold of her body—that is, the substance of the physical world <note>original: "third Principle"</note>—and changed it into its own property: the *power* of the first Principle, which was the most dominant force in her body. It was according to this property that she was seized in the *Disturbance* <note>original: *Turba*</note>.

30. We should not consider this a strange thing, for we find many examples of it in Scripture. Let us look at *Uzzah*, who was seized and struck down by the *Ark of the Covenant* when he only touched it, because the wrath of God was moved in the *Sound <margin>* That is, awakened and stirred up, and not atoned.</margin>. Let us also see how it seized the *Philistines* when they had the Ark of the Covenant with them; or how it devoured *Korah, Dathan, and Abiram* through Moses in the wilderness. All of these have the same origin, but each is manifested uniquely in its own way, depending on how the *Disturbance* <note>original: *Turba*</note> is kindled among the "three first" properties.

31. But

# CHAPTER 45: Of Abraham's Pilgrimage (Genesis 20)

### CHAPTER 45.
### How God led Abraham very wonderfully, and how he always stood by him in temptation and defended him; and what we are to understand by this.

<margin>Genesis 20</margin>
1. Abraham was to be only as a pilgrim upon the earth, traveling from one place to another and dwelling in tents. He was tested and tempted everywhere. His wife Sarah was twice taken from him but was wonderfully protected and preserved by God—once by Pharaoh in Egypt and then by Abimelech, King of Gerar. Both times, God protected her.

2. And now that Abraham—that is, the "stock" or origin of the conceived *ens* <term>original: "Ens of faith"; a Latin philosophical term meaning "essence" or "being," here referring to the spiritual seed or substance of faith</term> in which Christ was understood—had to wander from place to place and could have no permanent home on earth, and moreover lived in fear and temptation, this serves as a true type <term>A "type" is a biblical person or event that foreshadows a future reality, specifically Christ or the Church.</term> of Christianity on the earth. It shows how Christianity should not be bound to any certain place, nor to any specific people that God chose in a unique way, but that Christ, with his Gospel of the Kingdom of God, was given to all nations.

3. It also shows how he would travel with his knowledge from one people to another and have no constant home with any one nation, but remain among the nations with his children upon the earth only as a sojourner or stranger. It shows how people would continually try to destroy Christianity <margin>The true Christians.</margin> among the nations and cast reproach upon it, just as they sinfully insulted Sarah, Abraham's wife.

4. Furthermore, it shows how Christians would be continually tempted and tested by the nations, and plagued with conflict and war. It illustrates how Christ would move with his Gospel from one people to another when they became weary and bored with it, treating it only as a custom or a common, ordinary thing. In doing so, they would become completely blind to it, performing only a fine, devout "lip-service" <margin>A work of chatter and fair-sounding speech.</margin> and supposing they could find Christ through their sharp arguments and disputes.

5. Then he would depart from them with his understanding and spirit and come to another people, who would also be merely worldly <note>original: "fleshly"</note>, looking upon Christ externally as a mere man. This is just as Pharaoh and King Abimelech looked upon Abraham and his wife; they desired to have physical knowledge of Sarah because of her beauty. This signified that they would try to "put on" Christ physically in an outward, animal-like manner, but not in power and spirit.

6. This is seen here in Abimelech and also in Pharaoh: when they desired to know Sarah physically, the Lord intervened with punishments and plagues. He showed them his angry face, shut them up, and terrified them as if he had bound them with the chains of his power. He made their women barren and terrified them with visions and omens, as he did to this Abimelech, and threatened him with...

### CHAPTER 46.

#### Of Isaac's birth, and the casting out of Ishmael, with his mother Hagar: What is signified by this.

Genesis 21. The Spirit in Moses sets the figure <term>figure</term><note>A symbolic representation or spiritual type that foreshadows a later reality, like Christ.</note> of man's regeneration in its process so exactly and orderly together in the history of Abraham that a person may even lay hold of it—much more see it—how he sets the natural man in "self," and Christ, so precisely by each other; and points even with the finger at the figure. For when God had destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, and that plain over against which Abraham lived, and brought forth Lot, then Abraham journeyed from there toward the South. This shows that when the Kingdom of Christ is <margin>Corrupted.</margin> despoiled <note>original: "despoyled"; meaning ruined or corrupted</note> in any place, then Christ will depart from there.

2. And he lived under the King Abimelech and stayed as a stranger at Gerar. In these two names, namely Abimelech and Gerar, the figure stands plain in the generation or formation of the word without any interpretation or exposition; this is why the Spirit in Moses wrote down this history, through which he looks as if through an exact perspective <note>meaning a telescope or a clear lens</note>. For **ABIMELECH** denotes the man of ingenious and discreet reason—namely, the true man, but without Christ; only in the creaturely state as he is created. **GERAR** betokens the strong, austere life of nature in which the understanding must live. This nature is corrupted, and from that corruption it continually casts or darts temptations and oppositions into the life's understanding, or reason-light. Thus, the life stands in a constant contrariety and is incessantly sifted, winnowed, and proved, which is the <margin>Note.</margin> cross of the children of God. They see that while they live in themselves in self-reason, they can do nothing else but go astray, slip, and err, as may be seen here in Abraham. **CHAPTER XLVIII.**
***How God tested Abraham and presented the figure of Christ's offering in his suffering and death.***

[margin]Genesis 22[/margin] After the Spirit in Moses had deciphered the figure of the Covenant of God, established in Christ Jesus with his children—showing how we poor children of **Eve** should and must depart out of this earthly will of self-centeredness <term>original: "selfness," meaning the ego or self-will</term> and be born in Christ with a new will and life—he now sets forth the **figure** of how the same should and must be brought to pass. He shows how Christ must again offer up our soul and humanity to his Father, even as he also was to be cast as an offering into the fire of God's anger, and **wholly** die in the wrath of God to the human soul’s self-centeredness and own will. Yet, he would spring forth powerfully with the **divine** only will of God through death and the anger of God, and break in pieces and make a mockery of death, which held humanity captive. So he brings the **human soul** again to God his Father into the only eternal divine will, and **deliver up the kingdom to him again** [margin]1 Corinthians 15:24[/margin] which he had given him in humanity, so that afterward, and for all eternity, **God might be all in all** [margin]1 Corinthians 15:28[/margin] and the creature might not live any more to its **own** will, but be found only as an instrument of a divine tune in a divine harmony, and the whole human tree might be only **one** in all its boughs and branches.

2. The Spirit in Moses sets forth this figure very clearly, even to the end of all his writings, and plays, under the **outward** figure, with the **inward**, which shall remain forever. I will therefore set down this figure of **Abraham’s** temptation in respect to his son **Isaac**, likewise in the **spiritual** figure, and show what is thereby to be understood. For although the learned have **interpreted** it to mean that God tempted **Abraham** to see if he would continue steadfast in faith in Him, it actually has quite another meaning and interpretation. [margin]Note:[/margin] For God **knows** well **beforehand** what man will do; also, man **cannot** stand in temptation without His grace, as may be seen here in **Abraham** when he denied his wife before King **Abimelech** as he came into **Gerar**.

3. **Abraham** is here represented in **Adam’s** place, and his son **Isaac** is represented in Christ’s humanity, and the voice which came to **Abraham** is **God the Father’s**. These three stand here in the figure of the process of the work of man's redemption, showing how **Abraham**—that is, **Adam**—should offer up his [margin]Text. Image:[/margin] person in **Isaac**—that is, in **Christ**—to the voice of God in the **fire** of God, so that humanity might be proved in the fire of God.

Genesis 22:4. 11. *And Abraham said to the two young men whom he took with him, "Stay here with the donkey; and I and the lad will go over there and worship, and come again to you."*

**The internal symbolic meaning stands thus:**

The two young men must stay behind with the donkey and not go, at this time, to the offering; only Abraham and Isaac must perform that. This means that we poor children of Eve must remain with the first and third <term>Principles: in the author’s philosophy, these are the different levels of reality—the spiritual world of fire/will and the physical world</term> of our life—this time we spend with the "donkey," meaning the *outward body* here in this world. He alone was to go and offer up the sacrifice of his body to the "anger-fire" <note>original: "Anger-fire," referring to God's divine justice or wrath</note> of his Father, and worship God his Father on our behalf. Therefore, he said he would go "yonder"; that is, when he was to offer up his life, he would go there to God and *worship for us*.

12. This refers to his *Ascension* according to his humanity. When he had finished the sacrifice, he went *there* <margin>*Yonder, or to that place</margin> and worshipped God his Father in our assumed humanity. This means that our assumed soul, through divine power and property, prays and intercedes before God for our *weaknesses* and *ignorance*. Therefore Abraham says, "we will go yonder and worship"; that is, "we"—God and Man together. "And when we have worshipped, we will come again to you." This means we poor children of Eve must meanwhile *wait* with the donkey until the time of the offering and prayer is finished, and then he *comes again* to us, once we have finished the course of this *outward, donkey-like* <note>original: "Asinine," referring to the physical, animalistic nature of the body</note> life.

13. Therefore, do not consider this an uncertain fiction; the Morning Star and the messenger of the announcement has appeared.

### CHAPTER 48. *Offering his Son Isaac.* Genesis 22. 339

The precious symbolic figure is this:

The Spirit here acts in Christ’s person, who had come in great humility into Adam’s humanity. He presents himself to his father in Adam’s essence, with his heavenly humanity, and says: "Behold, my father, here I have taken on the sin and death in the humanity. This is what God would reveal in the essence of faith within our disappeared and heavenly humanity. He said God would provide himself a lamb for the *true* burnt offering, and by this, he secretly points to the heavenly humanity which God would introduce into Christ’s humanity (which is our humanity). This would be the *patient Lamb* that God would provide for himself, which Abraham had already apprehended and hinted at through faith.

It is called a *twofold cave* because there are two mansions, namely <note>original: "viz."</note> a twofold container of life in two principles, from which man did originally arise. But if he is buried in the will of his selfhood in the serpent's desire, then he does not reach this twofold cave; and though he should be in it, he lives only in the apostate essence in the "ownhood" <note>original: "ownhood"; refers to the state of being self-centered or living for one's own private interests rather than God's</note> of the Devil—namely <note>original: "viz."</note> in the introduced serpent's essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> in the dark world's property, which is manifest and predominant in the serpent's essence <note>original: "Ens"</note>.

14. The chief part of this figure is that the spirit of *Moses* points at the twofold life, and how this world has a twofold life and essence. He intimates this by the twofold cave where *Abraham* would have his burying place, to signify that his twofold humanity should be buried and put into an eternal sepulcher. This humanity consists of one part from the *divine essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> out of eternity and heavenly spiritual essentiality, and another part which is out of time, even out of this world’s being and substance. There, the substance of the twofold body shall lie in its *original* Mother and leave the own-will in this *eternal grave* in death, so that the spirit of God might alone live, rule, and will in the spirit of the creature—namely <note>original: "viz."</note> in the soul. Thus, the life of man might be only His *instrument* with which He might work and will how and what He pleases.

52. When Christ has married himself to Virgin Sophia—that is, with the *inward humanity*—soon after, the voice of God sounds in the soul and says, "I will go away from you with the virgin." It is continually as if he would withdraw and depart from the person. Then the poor soul must offer continual prayers and supplications that he would be pleased to stay even longer with it. The inward meaning is this:

55. It is ashamed that it has lain so long captive in the bestial <note>original: "beastiall"; meaning animal-like or carnal.</note> man, and that it was a queen but lost its kingdom in Adam. Then the soul veils its own face before God's glorious brightness <note>original: "Clarity"</note> and humbles itself. But Christ takes her into his arms and leads her into his mother's tent—that is, into the essence of the heavenly world.

8. And just as Abraham’s *natural* children were not *disinherited* from the *Covenant*, but only from his *goods*, so likewise no person is disinherited from the Covenant of God established in *Adam* and *Abraham*. *Every person receives the freely given Covenant in the womb*; in this freely given Covenant, they have the power to turn toward Christ’s spiritual goods.

9. But a person does not possess these goods by the *right of nature*, as if they could take them by their *own* will; rather, they are a free gift. They shall and must resign themselves to the Covenant as a servant, completely giving up their own natural will to the Covenant. They must *forsake* the will that claims a "right of nature" and become entirely the Covenant’s own. In this way, they no longer introduce their own *natural will* into the Covenant and free gift, but surrender their will to the Covenant. Then the free gift stands in the place of their own will, and the nature of *Adam* lives in the free gift and also enjoys the inheritance—not through self-will, but in true resignation <note>original: "Resignation," referring to the spiritual practice of *Gelassenheit*, or the soul's surrender of its own ego to God's will</note>, where the *will of the Covenant* becomes the person's will.

10. For the *will* of the Covenant inherits the sonship by the right of nature, but the will of the natural selfhood is cast out from it. That self-will must die to its "own-hood" <note>original: "assuming own-hood," the state of the ego claiming ownership over itself and its actions independent of God</note>. When this is accomplished, it arises in the Covenant in Christ and possesses the free gift by the *right of grace*. Christ has manifested himself in the Covenant—in the gift freely given to *Adam* within human nature—and has become the life and will of the Covenant and *fulfilled* it.

11. But now this freely given Covenant, which God bestowed on *Adam*, lies within all people. For just as sin passed as a birthright from one to all, so also the Covenant and the free gift of grace pass from one to all. *Every person has Christ within them*; but their own will does not perceive him. Instead, it *crucifies* him and will not die to its own selfhood so that it might enter into Christ’s death and arise in the Covenant in the will of Christ.

12. The own-will desires only to be an externally adopted son of grace, and yet it is cast out from the presence of God. Just as *Abraham* cast out his natural children from his goods and disinherited them, giving the goods *only to Isaac*, so likewise the kingdom of God belongs *only to the will of the Covenant*.

13. Which indeed lies within all people, but no one can receive or see the kingdom of God unless they become a *child* of the Covenant. They must forsake their natural, outgoing will and put on the will of Christ in the Covenant, so that their will in the Covenant is *born anew* <margin>John 15:5</margin> in Christ. Then they are *a branch on the vine of Christ* and receive Christ’s spirit, will, and life. Regarding the Covenant, they become *Christ* <note>The author uses "Christ" here to mean "an anointed one," derived from the Greek *Christos*</note>; thus Christ then dwells in *Adam* and *Adam* in Christ. 14. But the fact that *Abraham sent the children of his Adamic nature away from his house with gifts*, rather than keeping them with him as residents, signifies that the external person *will*, while in this life, live in the will of the self upon the earth. They cannot completely put off that self while in the *earthly man*; but this same earthly self-will is cast out from the holiness of God—that is, from the kingdom of heaven.

27. It is not he who has the *words* and title of the law that is a *Jew* born in the foreshadowing and in the law, but he who is born of the *promise* in *Abraham’s* faith. He who lives in the foreshadowing of Christ—namely, in the law in profession and *practice* (with both mouth and heart)—the same, the *law* of God in *Christ's* foreshadowing has understood, and will bring him into the *fulfilling* of that foreshadowing.

28. For it does not only depend on a person's *knowing* that Christ has given himself into the law and has become the *fulfillment* of the law, as the <term>titular Christian</term> <note>A person who is Christian in name only, without active faith or practice</note> boasts. Instead, it depends on God's <margin>Ordinance.</margin> order and on the mercy of God. Whosoever has been a *true Jew* and has put on *Abraham’s faith* in the law, he has put on the <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term meaning "being" or "essential substance." Böhme uses it to describe the spiritual substance of Christ.</note> of Christ, which *Abraham* conceived or understood. The humanity of Christ has fulfilled this *Ens* of faith; and it is hidden from the Jew what it is, for he works in the office of nature in the *law* of God, which Christ has taken into himself and fulfilled. So, he serves God in the *office* of nature, and the *office* of nature serves Christ, for it has become *Christ's* own property.

29. For *unto him all power is given both in heaven and on earth* (Matthew 28). Under this power, the office of nature is also found within the law. For God, in the spirit of Christ, is the very same who *gave* the law and the office of nature to do *righteousness*, together with the foreshadowing of the kingdom of Christ and the *Ens* of faith to *Abraham* and *Moses*. He is also the very same who fulfilled the faith and the law.

30. Thus, the Jew works in his faith in *Christ's office*—namely, in the *Law*—with which Christ governs in nature. He has put on Christ in the *Covenant* and in the *Ens* of faith in *Christ's foreshadowing*, which Christ has fulfilled.

31. For the Christian who confesses Christ in the flesh works in his *faith* in the flesh of Christ and has the *law* of nature—God's officer—to act uprightly in his faith. For Christ rules in the Law of God, which he has fulfilled and made a servant in his children. He *kills* the law of *sin* through the fulfillment of his love in his *blood and death*, both in those who live in the dominion of *his Law* and also in those who live in the dominion of *his victory*, as the Christians do.

32. For the faith which presses or comes in unto God in the law, in the foreshadowing, and in the Covenant, is the same faith that comes unto God in the *Ens* of *Abraham’s* faith, out of which Christ was born. And he that comes in unto God in the *fulfillment* of the same does come or press in to God in the *humanity* of Christ—namely, in the whole process of his suffering, death, and resurrection.

How then, if anyone despises and condemns his brother who does not yet have his knowledge, can he boast of the love of God? For with that love, God loved his enemies in Christ, and with that love, Christ prayed for his enemies.

# 370 Genesis 25: The History of Isaac. Chapter 51.

Isaac’s life is a pattern showing how human nature and the created being have dwelt by the wellspring of the divine <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; Latin for "being" or "essence"</note> in the Covenant which Abraham embraced through faith. Specifically, Isaac’s soul lived by the wellspring of the Holy Trinity, in which the soul received its light and saw and knew the will of God. Out of that wellspring, the highest love of the Deity manifested itself to the soul. From that same [unclear marginal note] fountain, later in the fullness of time, the holy name Jesus—arising out of Jehovah—manifested itself and betrothed itself as a Bride to the soul.

2. Isaac's soul lived by this fountain of the "living and seeing" until that same fountain later poured forth and opened itself within the soul through the humanity of Christ. After that, the soul lived in the fountain once it was exalted in Christ’s person to the right hand of God. Then, the fountain of God sprang forth through the [unclear marginal note] soul, where it received the divine light as a "Prince of God" <note>A reference to the name "Israel," often interpreted as "Prince of God."</note>, or as an image and express likeness of God—a formed word of God’s voice through which God was made known and manifest.

3. Similarly, when our soul abandons the earthly will of its own assumed self and takes hold of the <term>Ens</term> of Christ in the Covenant and turns itself toward God, it also lives by the "fountain of the living and seeing." That is, it lives by God’s Eye, which he has again manifested and opened in humanity through Christ. Indeed, in this present time of our "earthly cottage" <note>A metaphor for the mortal human body.</note>, our soul does not inhabit the wellspring of God as if it could contain the wellspring within its own self. Instead, it is like the sun shining through glass: the glass is not transformed into the sun, yet it lives by the [unclear marginal note] luster and virtue of the sun, allowing the sun to work and [unclear marginal note] shine through it. This is how the soul is during this life.

4. Furthermore, just as the sun imparts its <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincture"; in Jacob Boehme’s thought, this refers to a spiritual quality or vitalizing power that transforms substance.</note> into a metallic essence, and the metallic essence gives its desire into the sun’s [unclear marginal note] <term>Tincture</term> so that fair and precious gold is generated from them both, the relationship between the soul and the fountain of God is understood in the same way. The Deity inhabits the soul, but the soul does not <margin>Or, dwells through the soul.</margin> grasp the Deity by its own creaturely power. Rather, the Eye or light of God, carrying the holy "Love-tincture" from the luster of that light, gives itself into the desire of the soul.

5. <margin>Note what the **Fiat** is.</margin> For the desire of the soul is the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "Let it be done," referring to the creative word or command of God.</note>, which takes the power of the holy Love-tincture into itself and makes it substantial. Thus, the divine tincture proceeding from the desire of the true Love-spring (namely, from the "fountain of the living and seeing") and the soul’s believing desire become one Essence.

6. Understand this as a spiritual Essence. This same spiritual Essence is the "inward new man"—a new house or habitation for the soul in which it lives according to the inward heavenly world. The name of this Essence is **Sophia** <note>original: "Sophia"; Greek for "Wisdom," representing the divine feminine or the "Bride" of the soul.</note>, the Bride of Christ and Christ’s humanity. In this Essence, the glorious Star of Jacob <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 24:17, symbolizing the Messiah.</note>—the dear and precious name of Jesus—is a shining light by which the soul sees and knows God.

7. The soul is not changed into the Deity itself (that is, into **Beer-lahai-roi**, the [unclear marginal note] fountain of the living and seeing), for the soul consists of eternal and temporal nature. The Deity is not nature itself, but rather the *will* toward nature; it manifests itself through the soul’s nature, just as fire manifests itself through...

# Chapter 52 and the birth of Esau and Jacob. Genesis 25. 373

[Isaac loved Esau] more than *Jacob*; he did not love Esau's iniquity, but his child-like nature, to which he wished to do much good. Neither the Jews nor the Christians until now have had a right understanding of this, though it was correctly understood in its true meaning among the Patriarchs.

-># CHAPTER 53.<-

->How Esau despised his birthright, and sold it for a bowl of lentil stew; what we are to understand by this representation <note>original: "figure"; here referring to a biblical type or allegory</note>.<-

When the spirit of Moses had set down the birth of Esau and Jacob, <margin>Genesis 25, verse 29</margin> he proceeds immediately to relate how the natural, Adamic man would regard this high gift in the Covenant very little or not at all, and would only seek after the satisfaction <note>original: "Belly-filling"</note> of the earthly life, like Esau, who gave his birthright for lentil stew, so that he might only serve his stomach.

The representation <note>original: "figure"</note> of Moses stands thus:

2. *And Jacob cooked stew, and Esau came from the field, and he was faint;* <margin>Genesis 25:29 to 34</margin> *and Esau said to Jacob, "Feed me, I pray you, with that same red stew, for I am faint"; and therefore his name was called* Edom. *But Jacob said, "Sell me this day your birthright." And Esau answered, "Look! I am about to die, and what profit will this birthright be to me?" And Jacob said, "Swear to me this day," and he swore to him; and so he sold his birthright to Jacob. Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and rose up, and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.*

This representation <note>original: "figure"</note> externally has only a plain and simple <note>original: "child-like"</note> appearance; yet it is a representation of the greatest mysteries. For Esau signifies the first power of the natural, created *Adam*, and Jacob signifies the power of the other Adam, Christ; thus does the spirit play with the representation here.

3. For *Adam’s* nature came from the field and was *faint*, and longed to eat of the stew which Jacob had. *Adam* was a substance <note>original: "Limus"; Latin for slime or mud, referring to the "dust of the ground" from which man was formed</note> of the earth and a substance <note>original: "Limus"</note> of heaven; but since he died to the substance of heaven, the earthly nature had wearied him in its strife; and in this representation (of the faint *Adam*), Esau stood here.

4. The red lentil stew which Jacob had—after which the faint *Adam* in Esau longed—was the essence <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for being or essence</note> of faith, namely, the essence of Christ. The Adamic nature in Esau, in its anguish and toilsome labor, in its corruption and misery, longed after this essence which was in Jacob; yet the earthly nature of Esau did not understand it, but the soul's nature, which also longed after Christ’s essence, which was strange (or hidden far off) to reason.

5. Esau’s foolish nature said in its longing to Jacob, "Let me, I pray you, taste of the red stew; for I am weary and faint by reason of the *driver* <note>The "driver" likely refers to the harsh demands of the physical world or the stars/constellations in the author's mystical framework.</note>...

**CHAPTER 55. Of Isaac blessing Jacob. Genesis 27.**

**CHAPTER LV.**

*Showing what we are to understand by Isaac blessing Jacob*
*unknowingly when he was old and ready to die.*

**The Gates of the Great Mysteries of the whole Bible.**

1. When Reason reads this history in the 27th chapter of Genesis, <margin>Genesis 27</margin> it has a twofold theory about it. One is that Rebecca only loved Jacob more than Esau and therefore used trickery to help him obtain his father’s blessing. Furthermore, Reason assumes that this happened by the appointment and providence of God because Esau was not worthy of the blessing; therefore, Reason takes it upon itself to completely condemn Esau. Based on this, it has also established the doctrine of Predestination <note>The author is critiquing the idea that God arbitrarily chooses who is saved or damned without a deeper spiritual reason.</note>. And yet, Reason understands nothing at all about this wonderful symbolic figure.

2. Now, if we wish to rightly understand and interpret this figure, then we must place the Patriarch Isaac in the role of God the Father, who alone can bless, and who also blessed Isaac within Abraham's seed so that Isaac should, in turn, bless his own offspring in the line of the Covenant.

3. And Esau was placed in the role of depraved nature—that is <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, in the kingdom of corrupt nature—within the human condition as it is perceived through the anger of God.

4. And we place Jacob in the role of the new birth, within the humanity of Christ, which God the Father blessed instead of the depraved Adam when He brought forth a new generation out of our humanity through this lineage.

5. And we see here how Adam foolishly threw away and lost the blessing and divine <term>unction</term> (spiritual anointing), and how he was rejected by God in his earthly image. We see how he lost his right to the divine anointing, just as Esau here, the firstborn, also lost the blessing.

**The inward spiritual figure stands thus.**

6. Isaac was old and expected to die, and he called for Esau, his firstborn son. <margin>Genesis 27</margin>

<summary>This page provides a spiritual interpretation of Isaac blessing Jacob, arguing that the event is a symbolic "figure" where Isaac represents God the Father, Esau represents corrupt human nature, and Jacob represents the "new birth" in Christ.</summary>

8. Blessing must become a substance, namely man, in the kingdom of nature. The kingdom of nature was not capable of this [substantial blessing] through its own power and might, just as here Esau, in his kingdom of nature, was not capable of the Father's blessing.

9. For the kingdom of human nature was so poisoned that it had to be dissolved. Therefore, the blessing of God the Father turned toward the woman's *tincture* <term>spiritual essence or quality</term>—namely, upon the Adamic female *tincture*, meaning the light’s *tincture*. For the fiery *tincture* in Adam was awakened in wrath (that is, in the kingdom of darkness) and was made into an earthly image. In this earthly image, the heavenly image was swallowed up and killed <note>original: "mortified"</note>. Now, the blessing would come to help this disappeared heavenly image so that it might be brought to life <note>original: "quickened"</note> again in the blessing. In this way, the kingdom of nature, into which the image was incorporated, would be blessed, transformed <note>original: "tinctured"</note>, and regenerated.

10. Since two lineages <note>original: "lines"</note> went out from the seed of Abraham and Isaac—namely, Ishmael and Esau as the truly corrupted Adamic image, and Isaac and Jacob as the lineage of the Covenant in freely given grace—the blessing of God the Father manifested in Isaac turned toward Jacob. This represents the lineage of Christ, whom God has anointed, so that he might again anoint the first-born Esau—the first corrupted Adamic man. For the first Adam had lost the birthright given to him from the divine Word at creation and could no longer be blessed from his own center.

11. For the soul's will was broken off from the eternal Word of divine holiness and had surrendered itself to the center of the First Principle <note>In this context, the "First Principle" refers to the harsh, fiery source of nature before it is enlightened by love</note>—namely, into the wrath of eternal nature and into the separation <note>original: "SeVeration"</note> of the speaking Word (the state of opposition and contentious conflict). This is why Isaac blessed Esau with the word of strife when he said to him in the blessing: *“You shall live by your sword and break your brother’s yoke from off your neck.”* This signified that the corrupted nature in him had become a servant of God’s anger and must now carry and manage the combat that Adam had stirred up in the properties of life, becoming a servant to that struggle.

12. The fact that Isaac did not understand this, and intended to bless Esau with the blessing of the Covenant and give him the scepter in Zion, shows us that Isaac and all the holy children of God—though they are reborn through the new birth in the lineage of the Covenant—do not fully grasp or understand the internal foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> of their essence. In this internal foundation, the kingdom of God works and holds power, yet they cannot use it according to their own self-will. Instead, God directs this internal foundation of his dwelling place as he pleases, and the soul must simply observe what he does—just as Isaac had to see whom the Lord had actually blessed through him.

13. <margin>Genesis 27:4</margin> For Isaac said to Esau that he should prepare him savory meat, such as he loved to eat, and then his soul would bless him. However, this blessing remained within the lineage of the Covenant, from which Christ would emerge—not by the soul's power, but by God's power. For the soul of Isaac, and the souls of all Adam’s children, were still attached by their roots to the bond of God’s anger. This internal, indwelling lineage of grace was destined to destroy that anger through Christ's death and completely incorporate and unite the soul into the lineage of the Covenant.

14. There—

14. Instead, the light-tincture, which disappeared in Adam when the fire's might introduced dark earthliness into it, sprang forth again afresh in this Covenant’s line. Through the power of the inspoken and promised, incorporated Word of Grace, this same light-tincture held the might and power of the Blessing.

15. The "seed of the woman"—namely, the light-tincture and virtue—should bruise the head of the fiery Serpent and change the soul's fiery might into a meek love-fire. The fiery soul's will shall and must be wholly transmuted and turned into meekness.

16. This "disappeared light-tincture" was brought from Adam into the woman, namely into Eve. When it was in Adam, it was his fair Paradisiacal rose garden of specific love, wherein God was manifest. Now, being the figure of the new birth, it was represented in Isaac’s blessing. Therefore, his wife, the blessed Rebecca, also had to come forward as one who stood in the line of the Covenant. She set forth the right figure of Christ—namely Jacob—in the place of the blessing. This was to signify that Christ should be manifested in this Covenant’s line in the seed of the woman—namely, in the light- and fire-tincture—and take on the soul’s nature from the power of the light, so that he might rule over the fiery nature of the soul and change it into the power of the light.

17. Now Rebecca, Isaac’s wife, was here a figure of the Virgin Mary, who brought forth Christ—the blessed of God—who should bless Esau and all the Adamical children <note>original: "Adamicall"; descendants of Adam, or humanity in its fallen state.</note>. It was so ordered by the Lord that Rebecca should handle it this way, for she understood that the blessing—namely the scepter of Israel—rested in Jacob.

18. Because the "scepter in Zion" lay in the seed of the woman—namely, in virginity—the same scepter was also stirred here in the seed of the woman. Thus, a woman had to bring the Covenant’s line to the place of God the Father’s blessing, which was in Isaac. And the man’s will—namely, the soul’s natural fire-will—must step back and be a servant of God’s wonders, and see what God has done with him.

19. But though it appears to be a deceit or cunning subtlety that Rebecca instructed and urged Jacob to take away the blessing from Esau (as if she loved Jacob far above Esau), in this matter human reason is blind. For through the Devil’s cunning, the curse came into the world; and through the divine "cunning" in Love, the destruction of death and hell came again into the soul. The divine cunning killed the Devil’s cunning.

20. Understand it correctly: all cunning arises from the <term>lubet</term> <note>original: "lubet"; from the Latin 'libet,' meaning 'it pleases.' In Boehme's philosophy, it refers to the initial, subtle desire or "delight" of the will before it becomes a driving hunger.</note> or desire. The Devil’s cunning arose from the false *lubet* or lust. Likewise, God’s *lubet* came again into the woman’s seed (into which heavenly matrix the Devil had inserted his lust) and destroyed the Devil’s lust.

21. It was from God that Jacob obtained the blessing, wholly contrary to the mind and will of human reason; for he stood as the figure of Christ, and Esau stood as the figure of the depraved Adam.

22. There—

22. Therefore, Esau was a hairy or rough man, signifying the monstrous, animalistic nature <note>original: "beastiall property"</note> which had awakened in the Fall through lust. Now, when Adam’s lust had manifested itself into physical substance, the flesh became coarse and animalistic. Thus, the animalistic part swallowed up the heavenly part within itself, and death was manifested in the flesh; and we see here in this figure very clearly symbolized how it was meant to be.

23. Isaac wanted to bless the animalistic man in Esau, but God would not allow this; the divine blessing belonged to Christ. However, the fallen Adam could not be capable of receiving the blessing of God unless Christ took on this rough, animalistic skin for a form—the same skin that Adam had put on. For Christ had to enter into <margin>Note: *Isaiah 53:4; Matthew 8:17; 1 Peter 2:24.*</margin> our humanity, walk in our "hairy" form, and destroy the death caused by our animalistic nature; as it is written: *He took our sicknesses upon Himself and bore our grief.*

25. For just as Isaac took hold of his son Jacob in his hairy skin and felt whether he was his firstborn son to whom the blessing belonged, so God the Father reached into the essence of His Son, Christ, and felt whether <margin>*Note the cause of the Bloody Sweat.*</margin> the humanity of Christ was the original image created in Adam. Because of this, agony seized Him in the Garden of Olives, so that He sweat a bloody sweat, of which Isaiah speaks plainly: *He took our grief upon Himself.*

26. Therefore, His voice also rested upon Him during His baptism in the Jordan when He blessed our humanity, saying, *This is my beloved Son; listen to Him.*

27. So likewise, Isaac indeed heard the voice of Jacob under the hairy skin and understood that it was not Esau; yet the spirit in his blessing still moved powerfully upon him. For he sensed in Jacob the established foundation of the Covenant—namely, the lineage of the new humanity. For he <margin>*Genesis 27:22.*</margin> said: *The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.* By this, the Spirit suggests that in Jacob—and in all the children of God in flesh and blood—there is still the first fallen, animalistic, Adamic man with his hairy skin, which God does not look upon. Instead, He looks only to the divine voice, which is one spirit with God and inhabits the inner spiritual man <note>original: "Soul-ish-Man"</note>.

28. And then we see in this figure that our "beast's skin" of flesh and blood, in which we take such pride and make shows of devotion before God, is only a deceit. Just as Jacob stood as a deceiver before his father in this beast’s hide and intended to blind his father with the skin, so likewise the earthly man comes in his animalistic nature before God and desires God's blessing. But he may not obtain it unless he has Jacob’s—that is, Christ’s—voice within him under this beast's skin.

29. For just as Jacob was smooth and pure under this beast’s skin, so <margin>*Of the heart and soul.*</margin> must we be smooth, pure, and holy in our inward foundation, under this beast’s skin of ours, if we want the Blessing of God to alight and rest upon us.

18. God only in *one* manifest form, namely <note>original: viz.</note> in the darkness; but the properties shall be manifest only in the creatures themselves, each in its own peculiar self and *nature*.
For the formed *wisdom* regarding the darkness is the heaven of them all, which is only manifest according to the darkness, where the property lies *hidden*, according to which God calls himself *an angry, zealous God*. Out of this dark heaven, every creature receives its *power* and *virtue* according to its property; as its hunger is, so it sucks with its desire from there. And it signifies to us that the *unclean beasts*, each kind of them in their *form*, shall appear only in *one* form in the wisdom of the darkness—namely <note>original: viz.</note> in the *figure* as they were created in the beginning—and *not* in *seven* properties according to the center of nature in all (properties according to light and darkness) as the *rest* shall. For they are in the *figure* of the first Principle, which in the pure heaven shall be manifest *only* in one property—namely <note>original: viz.</note> according to the burning property in which the light is *moved* <margin>Movable and formable.</margin> and the wisdom is formed.

19. But here I will warn the reader to understand our sense and meaning correctly, and not to assume I am putting calves, cows, and beasts—in their spirit and body—into heaven. I speak only of the *eternal formed wisdom* from which evil and good have been brought to *manifestation*.

20. Moreover, God said to *Noah*: "*For yet seven days will I cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living substance which I have made will I destroy from off the face of the earth*." Why <note>original: wherefore</note> did God say the flood shall come after *seven* days? Why not immediately, either sooner or later? Why does he set exactly *seven* days? In this, the *seven* properties of nature are contained mystically, in which the *Word "Let there be"* <note>original: Verbum Fiat</note> had introduced itself into an *essence* <note>original: Ens</note>—namely <note>original: viz.</note> into the formed Word, that is, into the creation of the world. In this creation, the Formed Word *repented* at the vanity of all creatures and moved itself through the mother-source <note>original: generatresse; the productive or generative power</note> of nature, in the Formed Word, to *destroy the Turba* <note>term: Turba; a Latin term used here to describe a state of terminal confusion, wrath, or the "disturber" that leads to the destruction of a form</note>.

21. Now the first motion and formation <note>original: Information</note> of the Word in the creation—with the *six* days' works and the day of rest being *seven* days—was brought into a form of *time*, and it still stood so in its form. Then, when the *Word* (which said it would drown every life with water) did open, disclose, and manifest itself through the *seven* properties of nature toward the *water-birth* <note>note: This refers to the manifestation of the Flood as a natural/spiritual event</note>, it happened in the *form* in which the Word had given itself in the *creation*—namely <note>original: viz.</note> in the same *sevenfold operation*. This should open itself in its own peculiar *order* and not ignite or elevate any one property above the other. But if all *seven* would open and manifest themselves according to the *water-birth*, then the *only* fountain or headspring of all the depths in the center of nature would break open. And since they came into their outward formed working dominion in *seven* days, the speaking Word *also* proceeded in the opening of it over *seven* days, until the limit for its manifestation of what it desired: namely, to drown the *Turba*.

### CHAPTER 32. *Between God and Noah.* Genesis 8. 199

29. There is a very great mystery in what the Spirit says through **Moses: Noah was five hundred years old when he fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth**, which otherwise is against the ordinary course of nature, to father children at such a natural age. Also, there is a very great mystery in that God said that **he would give the world a hundred and twenty years’ respite, and yet the Deluge came in the six-hundredth year of Noah**, namely, in the hundredth year after the warning or notice of it. It signifies the abbreviation of time <note>original: "abbreviation of time"; the idea that God shortens the duration of an era to hasten judgment or salvation</note> in its natural course, and also the **End of the world**, how there shall be an abbreviation or shortening of time in the <margin>Query this treatise by itself.</margin> circle of the conclusion of all beings, of which we will mention something in a **treatise** by itself, if the same be permitted to us.

30. When **Noah** entered into the Ark, **Moses** says: **the Lord shut him in.** <margin>Verse 16.</margin> The intimate significance of the Spirit here is: He shut up the Second Time or Age of the world, which was at its **end**, since the fire would have gladly moved itself; therefore the Lord shut it up with water. Herewith He also [opened] the gate of his entrance to go forth into the **Third** time, and begin the **Second Monarchy** <term>Second Monarchy: a theological concept describing the second major period of human history under divine governance</term> in the outward world. For the **first** time was in **Paradise**; the **second** was under **Seth’s manifestation**; in the third, **Enos’s manifestation** <note>Seth and Enos represent stages of spiritual development in the lineage of Adam</note> should be opened and set forth.

31. And **Moses** says further: **and the waters stood upon the Earth one hundred and fifty days, then God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that were with him in the Ark; and God caused a wind to pass over the Earth and the waters subsided, and the fountains of the deep and the windows also of heaven were stopped.** <margin>Chapter 8, verses 1–3.</margin> Moses says, **God Remembered Noah**: now reason thinks, had He then forgotten him? Whereas He is present to all things, and is **Himself through all, and in all things.** The Spirit in **Moses** here hangs a veil before the mystery so that the natural man does not understand it.

32. God’s **remembrance** here is the beginning of the **Third Time**, even the beginning of the **Second Monarchy** in the four elements with the creatures. For in the Covenant made with Noah, the Second Monarchy was included, which went forth out of the center of the Generatress <note>original: "Generatreſſe"; referring to the creative or generative power of nature</note> through the divine wisdom in Nature.

33. And **Moses** speaks further: **when the waters were abated the Ark set itself down upon Mount Ararat.** <margin>Verse 4.</margin> This name [**ARARAT**] plainly hints to us in the language of nature <note>The "language of nature" is a concept where the sounds of words reveal the essence of the things they name</note> a **mountain**, or a compacting and a gathering of an essence out of the **center** of nature, even out of the wrathfulness, since the **anger** of God had then settled itself there. The Ark stood upon the **subdued anger**, but the last syllable in this word **Ara-RAT** signifies that the wrath of the eternal nature proceeding from the center has taken or formed itself into an **active dominion**, and would from then on ride through nature as a **warrior**. It would mightily exercise its power and violence in the human property, whereby they would undertake **wars**, and advance themselves in pride, pomp, and power, and butcher and slay one another, eagerly contending about this mountain of the wrath's might, or **severe human authority.**

34. This mountain **Ararat** denotes the houses of the **great ones**, or domineering potentates upon the Earth, namely, the great **castles, forts, and bulwarks**;

35. 43. The **first dove** signifies the **prophetic spirit**, which arose under **Moses**—namely, under the **outward Law** and **offerings**—and pointed through the offering into the Ark of **Noah** and **Christ**. 44. The **second dove** with the **olive branch**, which also came back to Noah into the Ark, denotes the Word in the **Covenant of Noah**. That it was an **olive leaf** denotes the **anointing** <note>original: "Unction"</note> of the Holy Spirit, signifying that the same Spirit should anoint humanity and bring it again with this dove into the holy Ark.

45. The **third dove** which Noah let fly, and which did not return to the Ark, signifies the kingdom of **Antichrist** upon the earth. This kingdom has indeed flown forth with its **doctrine** out of the Ark, but its **spirit** remains only upon the earth, feeding upon the **fat grass** <gloss>upon the riches, honor, and beauty of this world</gloss>. And so it stays only in self-interest <note>original: "Selfehood"</note> and does not return to the Ark. It indeed puts on **devout shows** of holiness to God and speaks good words, but the man, with his senses and reason, will **not forsake** the world and return again to the Ark. They build themselves **stately palaces** outside the Ark for the pleasure of the flesh, and are very **zealous** and devout in hypocrisy outside the Ark. They wish to be accounted children by an **external** credit <note>original: "Imputation"</note> of grace and adoption, but they will not enter into the Ark. Instead, they say, "**Christ** is in the Ark; he has purchased and paid for everything; we only need to comfort ourselves with that fact; he will **bring us in** well enough."

46. This is what the **third dove** denotes, for the Antichristian kingdom walks demurely in the shape of a **dove** and as a **sheep**, but it is only a figure and dark **shadow** of Christ’s kingdom, which consists in the Spirit in power and is really **in** the Ark.

While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease." Moses says that God smelled a sweet aroma and said in his heart he would not again curse the earth, or strike every living creature anymore, for man's sake. This is a symbol <note>original: "figure"</note> or mystical foreshadowing <note>original: "Type"</note>, as was mentioned before regarding the offering of Abel.

The "inward world" within the creatures sensed this, which hereafter would deliver them by its own peculiar offering from the corruption <note>original: "abomination"</note> of vanity, and set their form into the holy wisdom—that is, into the spiritual world.

5. When God blessed Noah through the offering proceeding from the Covenant, and commanded them to be fruitful, he gave them again the whole world, with all its hosts in their possession. All that lives and moves should be subservient to them and be their own; and he gave it all to them in common. He made no difference there between Noah and his children, no <margin>Master.</margin> lord nor servant, but he made them all alike—none noble or ignoble. Just as many branches and twigs grow out of one tree, and yet all together are but one single tree, so also he established the human tree upon the earth. He gave them all beasts, fish, and birds in common, with no distinction, restriction, or prohibition, except only that they should not eat their life in the blood, lest they should become monstrous in their life <margin>Or by eating the life of the beasts.</margin> with the bestial <term>animal-like</term> life.

6. God commanded them to rule over all the beasts and creatures, but in this place he gave them no specific domination or ruling power over one another. For all domination, lordly rule, and authority, by which one man rules over another, arises out of Ararat—that is, from or through the order of nature, according to its properties, according to the constellations, and the outward dominion of the princes under the constellations, or the *Astrum* <note>original: Astram; referring to the starry heaven or celestial influences</note>.

7. The true image of God has no other dominion in its members than the body has in its members, or the tree in its branches; but the bestial image from the stars and four elements makes for itself a dominion and government according to its "mother" <note>In this context, "mother" refers to the source or nature from which something originates</note>, from which it takes its rise and in which it lives.

8. Also, all laws and external ordinances which God has appointed for man all belong to the order of nature, namely <note>original: viz.</note> to the expressed, formed Word. God has given these to man as a property <term>a specific characteristic or possession</term>, so that he should rule within them with the inward spiritual man of understanding, according to the wisdom of God, and create for himself [laws and] order according to the spirit of wisdom.

9. Over these orders and ordinances which men make for themselves, HE [namely, the Lord] has set himself as judge, and has therefore appointed the Last Judgment to separate wrong from right. Whatever does not proceed from truth, righteousness, and love, and does not tend toward the same, the judgment of God is set against it. For such things are generated or hatched through the false spirits of darkness in the Great Disturbance <note>original: Turba Magna; a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the source of divine wrath or chaos in nature</note> and introduced into human nature as a false lust and subtlety; it is a stranger or "bastard wisdom" which shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

10. All royal and princely highness and excellency, together with all governments and dominions, arise from the order of nature. In the image of God there is no compulsion [no force, violence, or oppression], but only a purely free, willing, and desiring service of love—as one member in the body or one branch of the tree freely and readily serves the other and rejoices in the other.

15. God maintains the kingdom of nature as His order and has given it into the power of man so that he—*as God’s instrument in this world*—should sever the evil from the good and choose himself as a judge to pass righteous judgment upon the iniquity and malice of the false desire and lust *of man*. For he says: *Whoever sheds man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed;* <note>Genesis 9:6</note> namely, by the order and institution of nature. This does not mean that anyone should avenge himself upon others by his own selfish power or force of *arms*, but through the order of nature, through *God's Law* and appointment; the law itself is the true *avenger*. For God said, *I will avenge your life’s blood, and will avenge it upon every beast;* <note>Genesis 9:5</note> here He means by the order of His Law and its officers who officiate in the right and due execution of the same.

16. *Not that a prince or lord has power to shed blood without the Law of God;* if he does so, then the Law of God condemns him also to death. Here, there is no personal *selfish power* given over man’s blood, whether he be king or prince; for they are only *officers* over the order of the *divine Law*, and they ought not to go further than the command of God gives leave. Indeed, they have the *law of nature* committed to their charge as servants of the same, but they must deal therein only according to righteousness and truth, and not do anything through selfish (*covetous, proud, and envious*) desire. For God has created man in His own image; now the kingdom of nature in its offices has no power over this *divine image* to kill it, but the office or commission in God’s order *acts only upon the outward image of nature.*

Thus we are also to understand that the Father in His will, who freely gave us the Son, took on *one part* the garment of our sins' covering (typified by *Japheth*), and the Son on the *other part* covered our shame with the Father’s will (which *Shem* was a figure of).

25. For if *Christ* shall lay the covering garment upon our shame, then the *soul* must help; that is, it must give up and resign its will wholly into it. It must go backward with its will toward the bosom of the Father and no longer parley <note>original: "parley"; to debate or negotiate.</note> with itself in its own will and knowledge about how it goes or will go. Instead, it must take the garment in true repentance upon its shoulders and leave the other part upon the shoulders of *Shem*, namely, unto the true image of <margin>Or God.</margin> *Christ*, which is the precious, noble *Sophia* <note>original: *Sophia*; the Greek word for Wisdom, representing the divine feminine or the light of God within the soul.</note>.

26. Both of these take the heavenly garment and go backward to the Father; and though they cannot see how they go, yet they go in *faith*, trusting in God’s mercy. They turn away their eyes from the shame, vanity, and false wills; for going backward and covering the shame in this place signifies nothing else but to *convert* the selfhood that naturally goes forward in its own will and way, and to go back again into the ONE, out of which the free will departed and entered into the monster, or shame.

27. *Noah’s* drunkenness signifies that when *Adam* entered with his lust and desire into this world’s property, he became drunk in the bestial <note>original: "beastiall"; relating to the animal nature as opposed to the spiritual.</note> property; and therein he uncovered his shame. That is, he disclosed and made bare the bestial *lust*. Now when this was done, he stood before God in great shame; and then the bestial spirit in this monster of false lust and poisonous desire broke forth, insulted the precious heavenly image, and made itself master.

28. And thus Christ must, in our soul and in our disappeared and again revived noble *Sophia*, cover the shame of our father *Adam* and his children. For He would, therefore, not be born of the seed of man, but out of the heavenly disappeared *Ens* <note>original: *Ens*; Latin for "being" or "essence."</note>, and brought His living *Ens* of the holy world into it. He did this so that He might cover our monstrous <margin>original text: "Shame"; marginal note: "Seed".</margin> shame of the soul's property, which *Adam’s* lust had uncovered, with the heavenly *Ens*.

29. The corrupt nature which had now opened itself in Paradise continued in all men; and though the image of God was again regenerated in the spirit of the saints as a figurative form until the fulfillment of Christ in the flesh, yet the monstrous image was passed down...

# Chapter 34: Concerning Noah’s Cursing of Ham (Genesis 9)

[Page] 215

36. The Japhethites <note>original: "Japhites"; the descendants of Noah's son Japheth</note> were seen as a poor, disesteemed, rejected, and abject people; but the tribe of Japheth would present themselves with great, persuasive words and with a great and huge ostentation <note>original: "ostentation"; a showy display intended to impress</note> of God’s service. Yet, it would be nothing but hypocrisy and a seeming holiness proceeding from the light of nature. Meanwhile, Ham's lineage would be full of gluttony and drunkenness, scoffing and reviling; they would mock both the children of the Cain-like "seeming holiness" and also the children of the true light. They would live like wild, brute beasts; and yet, in their swinish life, they would claim to be "children of grace" through an outward appropriation <note>Taking something for oneself without a true right to it</note> or adoption.

37. This spirit of Ham now has dominion in Christendom. He has flattered Japheth so that, through the light of nature, he has set up an *external, showy divine worship* as a "titular god" <note>A god in name only, without real power or essence</note>. This titular god has covered Ham—in his beastly, Sodom-like spirit—with a very fair and glorious covering under the purple mantle of *Christ*. He has laid under his head great *sacks* <margin>* Or small bags full.</margin> *full of the light of grace*; and these the beastly "mouth-spirit" of Ham must take along with it. And indeed, when it must die, it thinks it has whole sacks full of the light of grace.

38. But the light of grace remains only in the sacks; Ham’s spirit remains in itself an evil beast and cannot truly open the sacks and take out the light of grace. This spirit of Ham is accursed and shall not inherit God’s kingdom unless it is *truly* born again out of the *light of grace*; otherwise, the sacks and coverings avail him *not at all*.

39. For a beast goes into the sanctuary (or to the holy service of God) and remains a beast when he leaves. Your "seeming holiness" and devotion—your comforting, flattering, and soothing of yourself—avail *nothing* unless you *return* again into your first mother from whom man originally proceeded, and *become as a little newborn child*. You must let Ham and Japheth go with all their *arts* and *idle talk* <note>original: "pratings"</note>.

40. For Japheth does not obtain it in his *showy*, glittering kingdom unless he enters into *Shem’s tent, namely* <note>original: "viz."</note> into the light of grace, so that the light may be born in him. Outwardly "adopted" children do not count in God’s estimation; only innate children, born anew of the heavenly <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical/theological term for "essential being" or "spiritual substance"</note> in Christ's spirit. And whoever does not have this is *already judged*. *John, Chapter 3.*

*Shows how the* <term>Human Tree</term> <note>original: "Humane Tree"</note> <margin>Or Tree of Mankind.</margin> *has spread itself through its properties by the children of Noah; and how they were divided and severed at the Tower of Babel in their properties, by the confusion of tongues, into distinct nations.*

[Large decorative initial E] VERY tree first grows (after it shoots out of its pregnant <term>seed</term> <note>original: "Seed"</note>) into a trunk, and afterwards into branches and boughs. <margin>Genesis 10. * Grain, kernel, or seed.</margin> It further brings forth from its <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ens"</note> the blossom and fruit. 2. Adam was the first essence for the grain (or the pregnant, fruitful seed of mankind). This same essence which produced human life existed within divine wisdom—in the word of the divine power of divine understanding. The Spirit of God brought this holy essence out of divine wisdom and <term>divine desire</term> <note>original: "lubet"</note> into the <term>Creative Word</term> <note>original: "Verbum Fiat," Latin for "let it be done"</note>—that is, into the desire of the forming word, or Nature. Within Nature, the Spirit of God shaped the essence of divine wisdom through the Speaking Word into a formal life. He also shaped the nature of the three principles into a body. Into this body (meaning the essence of nature), the Spirit of God breathed this same shaped, created life of divine understanding.

3. From this, man had his origin and became a living soul, arising both from the heavenly spiritual essence and from the temporary essence of the Earth and the four elements. He came from both the <term>star</term> <note>original: "Astrum"</note> of divine magic and the star of natural magic—a complete and perfect likeness of God. He was a delightful tree of the life of divine wisdom and contemplation, grafted into the paradise of God (namely, into heaven) and into the time of this world, existing in both. He was fit to <term>reproduce</term> <note>original: "regenerate"</note> <margin>To generate again or propagate.</margin> and form his own likeness from himself, just as many twigs, boughs, branches, and fruits grow from one tree. Every fruit contains a grain, kernel, or seed fit to produce a new trunk and tree; we should understand the tree of mankind in the same way.

4. The inward spiritual essence grew in its power within Adam's life until the outward, earthly, natural essence overcame him through the infectious persuasion of the Devil. Then, the natural essence forcibly asserted itself in the powers of the wonders of nature and brought forth its branches and boughs from the essence of nature.

14. 36. Great wonders! Just as the human tree has brought forth such wonders out of its sensual tongue—out of the many different properties of language—and introduced them into a *substance* for its growth and glory (namely, for the great harvest of God). In this harvest, each quality of love and anger, light and darkness, shall reap its own fruit. Every being shall possess its own heaven within itself, in its own formed and conceived *essence* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the internal nature or essence of a thing</note>, derived from the only Word of God. This Word has given itself to *every* life—even unto every life and being according to its own proper quality and virtue, and out of its own principle—as a *universal* word for the glorious manifestation of eternity.

37. Now, when we further consider this Beast with the *Whore* and what it is in itself, both inside and out, we find that it is the formed, rigid word of the "spirits of the letters" <note>The "spirits of the letters" refers to a literal, intellectual understanding of scripture and language that lacks spiritual life</note>. For men are *all* of *one only* quality regarding their life; all are begotten out of one flesh and soul, and all have only one kind of life. Like a tree with many boughs and branches, where the limbs and twigs do not seem perfectly alike in form, yet all have *one* only *sap* and *power*. So it is with the human creature among Jews, Christians, Turks <note>In this period, "Turks" was often used as a general term for Muslims</note>, and Heathens.

38. And the only *difference* is this: the "spirits of the letters" in the formed word *separate* us in our understanding. Otherwise, we all live alike in the *four elements*, eat the fruits of one Mother (the Earth), and remain in her when we die to this outward life.

39. The rigid, sensual tongue, which is divided into the spirits of the letters, *confounds* us and makes us wander. It makes us *suppose* we are strangers to one another, and yet we are all but one single tree. The Devil poisoned this tree with his desire in *Adam*, so that the equal balance <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect harmony or proportion</note> or harmony was brought into imbalance and discord. Consequently, the spirits of the letters were manifested in various ways, so that we speak with *many* languages. That is, we have introduced the powerful Word of God into the multiplicity of *divided* qualities. We have made, in the character of each tongue, a selfhood—a selfish desire for arrogance, self-importance, and entitlement.

40. Hence arise the conflicts, differences, and *opinions <margin>* Literal images or mental representations</margin>. These exist because we have introduced the unformed Word into the form of our own self-made image. Now we contend and strive about these *images* and conceits, and everyone supposes his own to be best. But when we bring all these images and various appearances back into one language and speech and *mortify them* <note>To "mortify" here means to kill off the selfish or ego-driven attachment to one's own opinions</note>, then the only *Quickening Word of God* <note>original: "Quickning"; meaning life-giving</note>—which gives power and life to all things—is again manifest. Then strife ceases, and *God is all in all*.

41. Therefore, we say as we have found it in the *grace of the One*: all human imaginations, opinions, and ways of knowing God (His being and His will) *outside of* the divine light <margin>* The certain anointing of the Holy Spirit</margin> are this same Whore’s Beast. It has flown forth and arisen from the rigid spirits of the letters, through which men contend about the literal meanings of those letters.

42. We have lost the *five vowels* in the alphabet, which introduce...

JESUS <note>original: "JEHSUS"; a mystical spelling often used to show the name of God (YHWH) being transformed by the letter "S" (Shin) into the name of the Savior</note>; and with his love, he has slain the *death* or deaths in the letters <note>original: "letters"; likely referring to the literal, external form of scripture or language which "kills" without the spirit</note>, and destroyed their self-will. He must give up himself without a will of his own, and leave himself *wholly* in God’s *mercy*. He must bring all his learning into this one only *thing*: that in his teachings and learnings, he will not do or speak anything but what God wills through him. And thus all images [opinions and conceits] *die* in him, and the soul’s life falls into the only *living word*, which has manifested itself again in humanity.

51. For this is the great *beast* of the Babylonian whore within us: that we bring ourselves into the images and forms of the letters and create *opinions* for ourselves. That *opinion* is a beast.

52. Also, we must not desire to know and will for ourselves, but die continually to our own self-will. In all things, we must give God the *honor* and give back to him that which he gives us—namely, whatever understanding, wisdom, and skill we have—and acknowledge that it is *not* our own, but that the divine Sun shines out of and through us, working in us as it pleases.

53. Likewise, we must spread and give out again our power and virtue <term>virtue: inherent power or divine efficacy</term>, which the divine Sun works in us, universally to everyone, without any gain, advantage, or *payment* from anyone. Whoever helps to maintain and nourish our life, we must be thankful to them, but we must not *flatter* anyone for the sake of their authority or receive their false appearance, show, or luster into this sunlight. Instead, all must be in general or common, just as the sunshine gives itself universally and gives no more to any strong, great, or potent thing than its purity and brightness; it tinctures <note>original: "Tinctureth"; in alchemy and mysticism, to infuse or permeate with a spiritual quality</note> the Earth and its children with one only power and virtue, and gives life and strength to all things.

54. In this, we shall *know* whether one is a teacher sent by God, or whether his origin and source are only from the spirit of the *letter*. If he is born universally out of *love*, then he has the light of *divine knowledge*, namely, the sensory divine understanding, a tongue tinctured...

Infused with the divine essence <note>original: "Ens", a Latin term for being or essence</note> of the five vowels, he speaks from the spirit of God. He rebukes and teaches powerfully without respect for any man’s person, and he has no image [or mental *idol*] in him; for he teaches from the Spirit of God, even what that same [spirit] teaches in him.

55. He puts himself forward with ostentation so that he may be known and honored; he wants to be applauded and set apart by men. He attributes understanding and wisdom to himself and boasts of his wisdom and a rectified judgment; yet he possesses none of them. He is only a builder of the Tower of Babel—that is, of an *external figure* and form. He is a *painted* Christian. He will undertake to teach others, and yet he himself was never taught by God. He teaches only from the form of the assembled spirits of the letter, which have gathered themselves in evil and good. He takes these into his own power and ability, and he compiles and sets the words together into an opinion.

56. And that opinion is the Tower of Babel.
