They will climb and ascend up to heaven upon this tower and are continually climbing throughout their whole life; yet they do not reach heaven through their opinion. But when the time of the outward, *literal constellation* <note>The "literal constellation" refers to the external, worldly arrangement of one's life or time</note> is finished, then this built tower falls down. The *outward* man, together with his opinion, shatters and breaks to pieces, leaving only the soul, which then stands naked and bare before God.

57. Here there is no remedy, unless the soul possesses the one and only spirit of the Sounding Letter <note>Boehme uses the "Sounding Letter" to refer to the living, spiritual essence of God’s word as opposed to the dead, written letter</note>—that is, the embodied <note>original: "enformed", meaning shaped from within</note> word of God—within it. If it does, it is able in its desire to attract and draw that word to itself and clothe itself with it. This word splits and breaks to pieces all the formed, contrived, and compiled tongues and *images* of the letters and brings them into one single tongue and will, which is *God all in all*. All things must enter again into the ONE—that is, into the universal. In multiplicity there is nothing but strife and disquiet; but in the Oneness there is an eternal *rest*, and no enmity or contrary will.

58. Now, when we truly consider again what the Tower and the *City of Babel* are in their physical form upon the Earth—what they are and where they are—then we find it clearly portrayed before our eyes. It is the great houses of the churches, cloisters <note>original: "cloysters", meaning monasteries or religious houses</note>, fortresses, and also the strong walls and towers of the cities upon the earth, where men hide themselves from force and power. In these opinions, they play the *hypocrites* before God.

...themselves images, who would set them at odds and variance about God? They indeed live and exist in the one and only God, and yet they contend and argue about God.

63. Why do they contend? They fight for the idols of their heart, for the stone houses of the churches, and for the pride of their images [and forged opinions]. Everyone wants to honor his own image and set it up high like a tall tower, so that he might be highly respected in the city of Babel <note>Babel, or Babylon, is used here as a symbol of spiritual confusion and false religion.</note>. Therefore, they build themselves strongholds and make great bulwarks and walls to defend and protect the image. They flatter themselves in hypocrisy, and by this contrived and painted image, they actually mean and understand the god *Maozim* <note>original: *Maozim*; a Hebrew term from Daniel 11:38 meaning "god of forces" or "strongholds," here interpreted as a god of material power and greed.</note>—namely, the fat-bellied god and the pleasure of the beast (that is, the image of this whore). They set the image upon the tower for the sake of showing off their holiness, appearing very devout in their glittering performances before God, as if serving a god they created themselves. But they lock the beast within their stone houses so that it may be secure, and there it grows fat.

64. What is this beast with the whore? It is half-devil, having its kingdom upon the earth, and it is half-beast. This evil beast has devoured man—namely, the *Image of God*.

65. And for this reason, God became man: so that he might destroy, slay, and nullify the works of the Devil. We must put on this divine humanity and destroy the Devil's kingdom within us, mortifying <note>term: mortify; to subdue or "kill off" sinful desires or false beliefs.</note> all images. Otherwise, we cannot see God; the living Word must mortify the literal image.

66. The living Word therefore became *man* so that the literal image might die, and so the first man—who was formed out of the living Word in God's image—might be born again in Christ's Spirit (that is, in the living Word). If a person is now born in this way, then all the "image-teachers" are more harmful than beneficial to him; for they only introduce their *images* into the temple of Christ and destroy the Image of God.

67. Let this be declared concerning the children of Nimrod <note>Nimrod was the biblical figure traditionally associated with the building of the Tower of Babel.</note> and the Tower of Babel, as the Spirit has given us to know. We admonish the reader, in love, to prove and examine himself; he shall find *where he stands*. 68. But the reason why so much is written concerning the beast and the whore of Babel is because she is at her *end* and shall soon be broken in pieces. ### CHAPTER 37.
**Of Abraham, and his seed, and of the Line of the Covenant in its Propagation; and also of the Heathenish Gods.**

1. If we look upon the history of the acts of the ancient, holy patriarchs with the right eyes of understanding, then we see therein nothing but wonders. For the lines [or races] of the children of God are like a tree which grows into boughs and branches until it bears fruit. Thus also the line of Christ grew in the *stem* of the promised word in the Covenant, from branch to branch, even to the height of the twigs, until its proper age, until the *power* of the tree—that is, the word in the Covenant—put itself forth with the glorious, *sovereign*, beautiful blossom.

2. Out of which blossom the holy Image of God is again grown in *flesh and blood, that is, in a holy body*. We see its boughs and branches are so fair and excellent that the soul rejoices most exceedingly at this contemplation, and truly desires to bud and grow forth along with these boughs and branches, to the great praise of God in our angelic tree of the *hierarchies of Christ* in the holy Paradise.

Moses also was no king, but a prince of God; this princedom continued until King Saul, whom the people desired as a king against God's command and will. CHAPTER 37. *Concerning Abraham and his seed.* Genesis 13. [Page] 255

47. For it is written in Genesis 18 that God appeared to Abraham in the form of three men and told him of a son who would proceed from his loins, whom Sarah would bear for him, upon whom the Covenant passed. Now, what did the appearance of these three men typify <note>original: "typifie"; to represent or symbolize beforehand</note>? It typified nothing else but the Trinity of the Deity and the manifestation of the divine, formed Word through the three principles. Therefore, the divine image was represented in three men, for it is a threefold essence <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for "being" or "entity"</note> but only one substance: namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, three worlds, yet within one another as one, but distinguished into three principles: namely, the dark, wrathful fire-world; the holy light-and-love fire-world; and the outward, visible world.

48. Out of these three worlds, man was created as an image of the divine manifestation. Therefore, God showed himself to Abraham in the same essence and substance, appearing in the form of an angelic message, yet speaking of himself.

49. For the represented essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> through which God spoke was both angelic and human, just as he would become human. For Christ, in regard to his created person, was to be a Prince or an angelic hierarchy. Likewise, God appeared to Abraham in this essential property <note>original: "Entall Essence"</note> with his own indwelling voice.

50. The history concerning Abraham is exceedingly wonderful, for the Kingdom of Christ is entirely represented within it—not only the kingdom upon the Earth in the time of the four elements (which is also portrayed and set forth beneath it), but yet only as a pilgrimage. This was not meant to be the true kingdom, for Abraham had to continually wander up and down, as did his posterity. Yet God promised him the country where he was a pilgrim as his own property, stating that he and his children should possess it eternally.

51. For God said to Abraham in Genesis 13: <margin>Genesis 13:14</margin> *“Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are: northward, southward, eastward, and westward; for all the land which you see, I will give it to you and to your seed forever.”* But they only obtained possession of this land a long time later, being first brought in by Joshua. Abraham and his grandchildren did not live to obtain it, and they were very often driven out from there. And yet, God said he would give it to Abraham and his children for an eternal possession.

52. But we see at present that they do not have it in their possession, for the Turks <note>Referring to the Ottoman Empire, which controlled the region when this was written</note> now possess it. Abraham's seed—namely, the Jews—presently have neither land nor princedom, but are in almost all places only as captives. However, the purpose of God must stand, and his word must be true: Abraham and his seed shall possess it eternally, for "eternal" is not merely temporal.

53. Therefore, God also spoke of the place and showed it to Abraham so that he might see it with his eyes. And even here lies the Great Mystery: for Paradise was in the world, and Adam lost Paradise; but in Abraham's seed—namely, in Christ—Paradise was restored again, not according to the mortal man, but according to the heavenly man.

54. Now we see at present that Christendom does not have these lands or countries in its possession, and likewise the Jews do not have them;

CHAPTER XXXVIII.

A clear explanation of the beginning of the heathenish war; how Abraham delivered Lot, his brother’s son; and of the Royal Priest Melchizedek of Salem, to whom Abraham gave tithes.

1. <margin>Genesis 14</margin> Here we see very clearly what the imaginations, purposes, intentions, and undertakings of men have been, even from their youth upward. We see how they have brought themselves out of the image of God into half-beastly and half-devilish qualities—namely, into pride, greed, and self-serving dominance—just as the Devil desired the same and was therefore cast out from his kingdom.

2. For here the Gentiles and the descendants of Ham at Sodom and Gomorrah, and in the whole region thereabouts, did now begin to exercise their domineering power. Abraham was only a stranger among them and lived in the Plain of Mamre as if in a wilderness, where he kept cattle. But the Gentiles fought and tore at each other for the kingdom of this world and for external might and power, striving for how one people might rule over another. Their will and dominion has continued even to this day, having received its beginning from the heathens and the descendants of Ham—namely, from Babel and from the confusion of languages <note>original: "divided tongues"</note>.

3. When the powers of the formed Word—that is, the properties of nature—divided themselves, and each part turned toward selfishness, then strife and enmity arose among them. This happened because the center of the nature of the dark world has obtained its dominion in the fallen character of man; for men were as if dead to the Kingdom of God (meaning love and humility) and lived at the time according to the outward stars and the four elements.

4. The Devil had also built his stronghold in the "serpent’s essence" <note>original: "Serpents Ens"; "Ens" is a technical term used by the author to describe the internal spiritual substance or being</note> within man. Therefore, they fought only for that which made them great and powerful in the world. And yet we may see how the Devil only fooled and mocked them <note>original: "Ape them"</note> within the wrath of God, so that they killed one another and valued temporary pleasure higher than their own lives. This is the greatest folly under the sun: that man should put his life in deadly danger for the sake of poor, foolish pride, even though he does not know whether he shall hold or possess that for which he murders, kills, and slays.

13. It is as the *heaven stands in hell*, and hell in heaven, and yet the one does neither confuse nor contain the other; or as the *night is in the day* and the day in the night; or as the light of nature dwells and shines in the darkness.

14. Thus we are to understand how the children of the Saints waged war against the crew of wicked men and drove them out—specifically, in the nature of *Anger*, which wielded its sword through them to destroy the heathens and the generation of *Ham*. For *Abraham* went out <margin>Genesis 14:14</margin> with his whole house and people against the heathens who had carried away *Lot, his brother’s son, captive*, and he struck the heathens and delivered his brother. This was done in the zeal of God, which thus delivered His children through the might of His anger; for what leads the wicked toward *destruction* leads holy men toward life and deliverance.

15. But as for those who would be called Christians (who ought, in and with Christ, to be dead to the anger and wrath of God through Christ's death) and yet wage war: they do it not as *Christians*, but as *heathens*. No true Christian wages war; for if he is a Christian, then he is *dead* in and with Christ’s death to the four elements of God's anger within himself. He is born as a new man in Christ’s spirit of love, who lives in righteousness, in love, and patience, and lives not for himself, but for God in Christ.

16. For a true Christian *directs his conduct <note>original: "conversation," meaning one's way of life or citizenship</note> and will in heaven*, in the life and Spirit of Christ, as Saint Paul says: *our conduct is in heaven*. But when Christians wage war, they do it from a *heathenish* nature and not from Christ’s nature. For a Christian is not of this world; his kingdom is in heaven, and he is dead in Christ to the world according to the new spiritual man within him. It is the heathen-man—namely, the *half-devilish* man (who has his kingdom in this world, who never has enough room upon the Earth, but lives in the four elements of God’s anger: Pride, Covetousness, Envy, and Wrath)—who desires, even in Christians, to war, fight, and slay.

17. Saint Paul says, *Give your members to be weapons of righteousness*; <margin>Romans 6:13</margin> for why do men fight? They fight for the kingdom of this world. <margin>James 4:1</margin> And yet, as Christ said, *His kingdom was not of this world*; <margin>John 18:36</margin> so also His children’s kingdom in Him is not of this world. Now then, if we give up our body and soul to be weapons of God’s anger and seek only our own self-interest, liberties, and the privileges of *wealth* <note>original: "Mammon"</note>, and slay one another for the kingdom of this world, I think we are indeed Christians in *speech*, but the *heart* and soul remain heathen and are not born out of Christ’s Spirit.

**CHAPTER XXXIX.**

*How God appeared to Abraham in a vision; and established the Covenant with him in his Seed <note>original: "Seed"; meaning his descendants or offspring</note>, and how Abraham’s faith laid hold of the Covenant, which God accounted to him for Righteousness, and how God commanded him to offer Sacrifice, and what is to be understood by that.*

<margin>Gen. 15. Verses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.</margin>

Moses says, *After these things it came to pass that the word of the Lord came to Abraham in a vision, saying: "Do not fear, Abram, I am your shield and your exceedingly great reward." But Abram said, "Lord God, what will you give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?" And Abraham said further: "To me you have given no offspring; and look, this son of my servant will be my heir." And behold, the Lord said to him, "He shall not be your heir; but he who shall come forth out of your own body shall be your heir." And he commanded him to go forth and said, "Look toward the Heaven and count the stars; can you count them?" And he said to him, "Even so shall your offspring be." Abraham believed God, and that was credited to him as Righteousness.*

2. In this portion of Scripture lies the root of the Christian Faith, for God said to *Abraham* that He was his Shield and Reward, and that He would give him the offspring out of *his own body*. God would be *Abraham's* reward and give him a son of his own, whose offspring should be as the stars in heaven, which are innumerable. Therefore she called the well where this was done "the Well of the Living One who has looked upon me."

21. This will would not humble itself under the Covenant and obey the Free One—namely, God’s only free will. Hagar fled away in this figure because the self-will must fly away and wholly die, and not inherit the Covenant and the adoption. But the Angel of the Lord met Hagar and said, "Where will you go, Hagar, Sarah’s maid? Return again to your mistress and humble yourself under her hand. 22. 37. For the children of Nature are servants in the Kingdom of Grace, not lords acting by their own self-will. They must not enter into the inheritance of the kingdom of Christ through their own self-will; for <margin>Romans 9:16</margin> *it does not depend* on any man’s own willing, thinking <note>original: "weening"</note>, running, or striving to desire and take the same by his own self-willed ability. 38. The mocker Ishmael had to be cast out from the blessed inheritance, for he was not born of the line of inheritance—namely, through God’s special gift as Isaac was. Isaac represented the person of Christ; for Christ alone was to be the heir of God’s blessing, holding it by right of nature. For Japheth must dwell in Shem’s <note>original: "Sems"</note> tent, not as a lord and master of the tent, but as a servant.

40. But for all others, the heavenly goods did not belong to them by natural right, for they had lost that right through Adam. ### CHAPTER XLII.
### Of the Three Men Who Appeared to Abraham in the Plain of Mamre; Who Went Toward Sodom, and Set the Cities of the Children of Ham on Fire from the Lord.

#### The meaning of this figure.

<margin>Gen. 18.</margin>
1. First, while Abraham was called only "Abram," God appeared to him in the vision as **One**. But when He had sealed the Covenant with circumcision, He called him "Abraham"—that is, a company or multitude of nations, a "forth-breathed" manifested people of God, in whom God had breathed forth or manifested Himself. He also appeared to him afterward in the manifestation of the holy Trinity—namely, in **three men** who were only **One**. In this, the manifestation of the holy Trinity within the Godhead <note>original: "Deity"</note> was set forth and represented in a human image, showing how the entire Trinity of the Godhead would now manifest itself in this Covenant within humanity, so that the Trinity of the Godhead should be seen **in the flesh**.

2. Hereby is declared the great humility of the Godhead, specifically in Christ; how Christ would visit mankind, care for man, and even condescend to be entertained by man. Just as He came in these three men to Abraham, allowed His feet to be washed, and ate and drank, this signifies that people must cherish and lovingly welcome the "poor Christ." He is "poor" in this world in His members and children, who would also be a poor, condemned, and despised people. Whatever people do unto them, they have done unto these three men—that is, to Christ, the holy Godhead in humanity.

<margin>Verse 1 to 16.</margin>

Of the Author
JACOB BEME <note>Jacob Böhme (1575–1624) was a prominent German Christian mystic and theologian whose work influenced later philosophy and Romanticism.</note>,
To his COMMENTARY upon

* MYSTERIUM MAGNUM. <margin>* The Great Mystery.</margin>

1. When we consider the visible world with its essence, and consider the life of its creatures, we find within them the likeness of the invisible spiritual world. This spiritual world is hidden in the visible world, just as the soul is in the body. By this, we see that the hidden God is near to all, and through all, and yet remains wholly hidden to the visible essence.

2. We have an example of this in the mind of man, which is an invisible fire inclined toward both light and darkness—namely, toward joy and sorrow. In itself, the mind is none of these things, but only the cause of them. It is an invisible, incomprehensible, originating fire <note>original: "Sourcive fire," a term Böhme uses to describe a fire that acts as the source or "welling up" of life and qualities</note>; and yet, as to its own essence, it is contained in nothing except only in the will of life.

3. The body cannot comprehend the mind, but the mind comprehends the body and brings it to love or * dislike; <margin>* Or suffering and sorrow.</margin> this is likewise how we should understand the Word and Power of God, which is hidden to the visible, physical elements.

...and yet dwells through and in the elements; and works through the sensible life and essence, as the mind does in the body.

4. For visible, sensible things are a manifestation <note>original: "eſſence"</note> of the invisible. From the invisible and incomprehensible, the visible and comprehensible has proceeded. The visible essence came into being from the expression, or the breathing out <note>original: "Spiration"</note>, of the invisible power. The invisible spiritual Word of divine power works with and through <margin>in</margin> the visible essence, as the soul works with and through <margin>in</margin> the body.

5. The inward spiritual soul of man was breathed into the visible image by the internal speaking <note>original: "in-Speaking"</note> or inspiration of the invisible Word of divine power (to give understanding to the created image). In this, man's knowledge <note>original: "Science," from the Latin *scientia*</note> and understanding of both the invisible and visible essence consists.

6. Thus, man has now received ability from the invisible Word of God for "re-expression"—that is, he expresses the hidden word of divine knowledge into form and representation <note>original: "setteration," likely meaning the act of positing or establishing a form</note>, in the manner and form of temporal creatures. He shapes this spiritual Word according to animals and plants <note>original: "Vegetables"</note>, by which the invisible wisdom of God is portrayed and modeled into several distinct forms. We plainly see that the understanding of man expresses all powers in their specific properties and gives names to all things according to each thing's nature <note>original: "property"</note>. By this, the hidden wisdom is known and understood in its power, and the hidden God is made manifest within <margin>in</margin> visible things for the delight and "play" of divine power—so that the invisible might play with the visible, and thereby introduce itself into its own sight and sense.

7. Just as the mind introduces itself into the senses and thoughts through the body, whereby it works and acts perceptibly to itself, so also the invisible world works through and with the visible world. We should not think in any way that a person cannot search out what the hidden divine world is, or what its operation and nature are; for in the visible essence of the creation, we see a representation <note>original: "figure"</note> of the internal spiritual operation of the powerful world.

8. And we ought not to think of God in any other way than as the most internal ground of all essences. Yet, he cannot be grasped by anything through that thing’s own power. But just as the sun introduces itself with its light and power into sensible living things and works in all things—bringing itself into a tangible form—the same is to be understood concerning the divine Word within the life of all creatures.

9. Seeing, then, that this visible world is the "expressed, formed Word," according to God’s love and anger—namely, according to the Grand Mystery <note>original: "Grand Myſtery," referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, a central concept in Boehme's cosmogony</note> of the eternal spiritual nature—this spiritual world is hidden in the visible. Furthermore, the human soul is a spark from the eternal, speaking Word of divine knowledge and power, and the body is a substance <note>original: "Ens," a Latin philosophical term for "being" or "entity"</note> of the stars and elements. Regarding its internal ground, the body is also a substance of heaven (the hidden world). Therefore, man has the might and ability to speak of the Grand Mystery from which all essences originally arise.

The first Chapter.
What God Manifested is: and of the Trinity.

1. 2. When I consider what God is, then I say: He is the One. In reference to the creature, He is like an Eternal Nothing <note>original: "Eternall Nothing"; Böhme uses this term to describe God as the *Ungrund*—the "groundless" or "bottomless" void that exists before and beyond all created things, forms, or definitions.</note>. He has neither foundation, beginning, nor abode. He possesses nothing, except only himself. He is the will of the Abyss <note>original: "Abyſſe"; the infinite, unmanifested source.</note>. He is in himself alone: one. He needs neither space nor place. He begets himself in himself, from eternity to eternity. He is neither like nor resembles anything, and has no specific place where he <margin>Or no separate habitation above the stars in an empyrean heaven, as human reason imagines.</margin> dwells. Eternal wisdom or understanding is his delight. He is the will of the wisdom; the wisdom is his manifestation.

3. In this eternal generation we are to understand three things: namely, 1. An eternal will. 2. An eternal mind of the will. 3. The <margin>Efflux, effluence, or the proceeding forth.</margin> outgoing <note>original: "Egreſſe"</note> from the will and mind, which is a Spirit of the will and mind.

# CHAP. 2. *Of the Word, or Heart of God.* 3

## CHAP. II.
### *Of the Word, or Heart of God.*

1. This is now what Saint John says in Chapter 1: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word; the same was in the beginning with God.* The word <margin>The word "In" signifies "within the."</margin> **"In"** is the will of the Abyss <note>original: "Abysse"; in Boehme's theology, the *Ungrund* or the "groundless" nothingness before creation</note>. <margin>Beginning (original: *Anfang*).</margin> **"Beginning"** is the conception (or apprehension) of the will, where it conceives and brings itself into an eternal beginning. <margin>The word (original: *Wort*).</margin> The **"Word"** is now the thing conceived, which in the will is a nothing; but with the conception, there is a generation <note>the act of bringing something into existence</note>. This was in the beginning with the will and in the will. But with the delight <term>original: "Lubet," a specialized term for the free desire or longing of the Divine Will</term> of the will, it receives its beginning in the conception of the will. Therefore, it is called a **Heart** <margin>The author explains these words in High German <note>original: "High-Dutch"</note> according to the "Language of Nature" <note>Boehme's theory that sounds and words reveal the inner essence of things</note>.</margin>—namely, a center or life-circle—within which the origin of eternal life resides.

2. And John says further: *By the same were all things made, and without it was not anything made that was made. In it was the life, and the life was the light of men.* Here, O man, take now this light of life which was in the Word and is eternal. Behold the Being of all beings, and especially yourself, since you are an image, life, and being of the unsearchable God, and a likeness to Him. Here, consider time and eternity; heaven and hell; the world; light and darkness; pain and source <note>original: "Source," likely translating *Qual*, Boehme's term for the agonizing tension or quality of being</note>; life and death; something and nothing. Here, examine yourself, whether you have the light and life of the Word in you, so that you are able to see and understand all things. For your life was in the Word and was made manifest in the image which God created; it was breathed into it from the Spirit of the Word. Now lift up your understanding in the light of your life and behold the **Formed Word**. Consider its inward generation, for all is manifest in the light of life.

3. Do you say, "I cannot; I am corrupt and depraved"? Listen to me! You are not yet born again of God; otherwise, if you had that same light again, then you would be able to. Come then! We all indeed come far short of the glory which we ought to have in God; but I will show you something. Pay attention and understand it rightly; do not be a mocker, as the confused Babel <note>A common term for the fragmented and arguing institutional churches of the time</note> is. Look! When we speak of the Being of all beings, we say that all things are from God and through God, for Saint John also says *that without Him was not anything made that was made.*

4. Now Reason says: "From where or how has God made good and evil, pain and joy, life and death? Is there any such will in God which makes the evil?" Here Reason begins to speculate and tries to understand it; but it only goes around the outside of the circle and cannot enter in, for it is outside and not in the Word of the life-circle.

...that you, with your outward *Spirit* and *Being*, are the outward world. You are a little world <note>original: "microcosm"</note> born out of the Great World. Your outward light is a mixture of the Sun and Stars; otherwise you could not see <margin>Or receive light from the Sun.</margin> by the light of the Sun. The Stars provide the *Essence* of distinction in your intellectual sight. Your body is composed of fire, air, water, and earth. Within it also lies the metallic property; for whatever the Sun and Stars are as a Spirit, the Earth and the other elements are as a <margin>Essence, substance, or body.</margin> Being—a solidified power. Whatever the superior [Being] is, the inferior is as well, and all the creatures of this world are the same.

6. When I take up a stone or a clod of earth and look upon it, I see that which is above and that which is below—indeed, I see the whole world within it. It is only that in each specific thing, one property happens to be the most prominent and manifest, and it is named according to that property. All other properties are jointly present within it, only in distinct degrees and centers; yet all these degrees and centers are ultimately but one single center. There is only one root from which all things proceed. It only divides itself in its <term>Compaction</term> <note>The process of becoming solid or physical.</note> where it is solidified. Its origin is like a smoke or a vaporous breath from the "Great Mystery" of the <term>Expressed Word</term> <note>The physical manifestation of God's creative speech.</note>. This Word stands in all places, constantly re-expressing itself—that is, re-breathing or echoing forth a likeness of itself: an Essence according to the Spirit.

7. But now we cannot say that the outward world is God, or the "speaking word" (which in itself is devoid of such physical essence). Likewise, we cannot say that the outward man is God. Rather, it is all merely the **expressed Word**, which has solidified itself in its own conception to become its own expression. It continues to solidify itself with the four elements through the spirit of desire (namely, the influence of the Stars) and brings itself into such motion and life. This happens in the same mode and manner that the Eternal Speaking Word creates a *Mystery*, which is *spiritual* in itself. I call this *Mystery* the *Center* of *Eternal Nature*. There, the Eternal Speaking Word brings itself into a "Generation" <note>A bringing-forth or birth.</note> and creates a Spiritual World within itself, just as we have a material world in the Expressed Word.

8. For I say that the inward world is the Heaven where God dwells, and the outward world is expressed out of the inward. It has a different beginning than the inward world, yet it still comes out of the inward. It is expressed from the inward (through the motion of the Eternal Speaking Word) and is contained within a beginning and an end.

9. And the inward world exists within the Eternal Speaking Word. The Eternal Word has spoken it (through Wisdom) out of its own powers, colors, and virtues, into an *Essence*—as a *Great Mystery*—from eternity. This *Essence* is also like a breathing from the *Word* within Wisdom, which contains its own "re-conception" into life within itself. With that *Conception*, it likewise solidifies itself and introduces itself into forms, following the manner in which the Eternal Word is generated. Just as powers, colors, and *Virtue* <note>In this context, "virtue" means inherent power or efficacy.</note> generate themselves in the Word through Wisdom—or as I might say, out of the Wisdom in the Word.

10. Therefore, there is nothing near to or far off from God. One...

# CHAPTER 3. Of the Center of Eternal Nature.

11. One world is within the other: and all are only one. The working Word is its life and is incomprehensible, for it is without any essence, being only like a mere understanding or a power that <margin>Or works itself out into the Essence.</margin> brings itself into essence.

## CHAPTER 3.
## How out of the Eternal Good, an evil has come to be, which in the Good had no beginning toward evil; and of the origin <margin>Or [unclear]</margin> of the Dark World, or Hell, where the devils dwell.

1. Now then, since light and darkness, and moreover pain and source <note>original: "Source" (German *Quelle*), referring to a "welling up," "quality," or "springing forth" of energy</note>, are seen in the outward world—and yet all originally proceed from the **Eternal Mystery**, namely, from the inward spiritual world—and the inward spiritual world proceeds out of the **Eternal Generating and Speaking Word**; we are therefore to consider how an evil has come to be out of the Eternal Good, which in the Good has no beginning toward evil. From where do darkness, pain, and "source" arise? And then, from where does a luster or light arise in the darkness?

2. For we cannot say that the **Eternal Light** or the **Eternal Darkness** is created; otherwise, they would exist within time and a comprehensible beginning, and of this they are devoid. For they are <margin>* Note.</margin> present together in the generation, yet not in the wisdom or generation of the **Word of the Deity**; rather, they take their origin in the desire of the Speaking Word.

3. For in the Eternal Speaking Word (which is <margin>Beyond or without.</margin> devoid of all nature or beginning) there is only the divine understanding or sound. There is neither darkness nor light, neither thick nor thin, neither joy nor sorrow; moreover, there is no sensibility or <margin>Finding or apprehension</margin> perception. Instead, it is merely a power of the understanding in one source, will, and dominion. There is neither friend nor foe to it, for it is the only Good, and nothing else.

Seeing then that this Eternal good cannot be an unperceivable essence (for if it were, it would not be manifest to itself), it introduces itself within itself into a *Lubet* <note>original: *Lubet*. In this *Lubet* is the wisdom. For the desire has nothing that it is able to make or conceive; instead, it conceives itself and impresses itself. It thickens <note>original: *Coagulateth*</note> itself; it draws itself into itself and comprehends itself. It brings itself from the *Abyss* <note>original: *Abyſſe*. This is the eternal original of the darkness; for where there is a property, there is already "something." <margin>Or causes darkness.</margin> And the *something* is not like the *nothing*: it yields obscurity unless something else—namely, a luster—fills it. Then it is light, and yet it remains a darkness within its property.

6. In this thickening, or impression, or desire, or hunger—by any of which I might express it to your understanding—I say, in this compaction or comprehensive complication, we are to understand two things:
1. The free *Lubet*, which is the wisdom, power, and virtue of the colors; and
2. The *desire* of the free *Lubet* within itself.
For the free *Lubet*—namely, the wisdom—is not a "property" <note>In this context, a "property" is a specific, limited quality or characteristic.</note> but is free from all inclination and is one with God. But the desire is a property. Now, the desire arises from the *Lubet*; therefore, the desire conceives and comprehends the free *Lubet* throughout the compaction and the impression, and brings it also into feeling and discovery.

7. Understand us correctly and precisely here: the desire arises out of the Will toward the free *Lubet* and makes itself out of the free *Lubet*; it brings itself into a desire. For that desire is the Father’s property; and the free *Lubet*—namely, the wisdom—is the <margin>Or One.</margin> Son’s property. However, since God is a Spirit, he is not called Father or Son in this place until the manifestation through the *Fire* in the Light. The *anguish-source* is to be understood this way: the astringent <margin>d. contracts</margin> desire conceives of itself and <insert>draws itself</insert> into itself, making itself full, hard, and rough. Now, the attraction is an enemy to the hardness. Hardness is retentive, while *attraction* is fugitive: one wants to go inward, and the other wants to go outward. But since they cannot *sever* or part from one another, they remain within each other like a *rolling wheel*: one wants to ascend, while the other wants to descend.

16. For *hardness* causes substance and weight, and the *compunction* <note>original: "compunction"; here meaning a pricking, stinging, or piercing sensation that initiates movement</note> gives *spirit* and the <margin>e. that flying</margin> *active life*. It is the greatest unquietness within itself, like a raging madness; it is in itself a horrible *anguish*. Yet no true feeling is <margin>f. or perceived / understood</margin> sensed until the *fire* <note>The fourth form, where nature is ignited into light or heat</note>—or the enkindling of the fire in nature, which is the fourth form, wherein the manifestation of each life *appears*. He shall find it in his own natural and ancestral knowledge.

17. The *anguish* creates the *sulfurous spirit*, and the *compunction* creates the *mercury*—that is, the *master-worker of nature*. He is the life of nature. These three properties impress the free *lubet* <note>original: "lubet"; a term for divine "pleasure" or the longing of the will toward manifestation</note> into themselves, so that it also provides a material essentiality. This is the oil of these three forms (namely, their life and joy), which softens, meeks, and allays their wrathfulness. No rational person can deny this; there is *salt, sulfur*, and *oil* in all things. And *mercury*—that is, the <margin>g. or poison-life</margin> vital venom—creates the essence in all things. Thus, the *abyss* brings itself into the *byss* <note>original: "bysse"; here meaning a structured foundation or measurable existence, the opposite of the bottomless abyss</note> and nature.

Thus, as *creatures*, we will write of the *properties*—namely, of the manifested God: how the *All* (that is, the *immense, abyssal, eternal* understanding) manifests itself.

Otherwise, if there were no *anguish*, then joy would not be manifest to itself, and there would be only one single will which would continually do the same thing. 10 [space] **Of the Two Principles. [space] CHAPTER 4.**

The free pleasure <note>original: "Lubet," from the Latin *libet*, referring to the divine longing or inclination of the soul or spirit</note>, which desires to be manifest, longs for the will of the Father, who has generated it without nature and uses it for his play. 25. Understand that it is the reconceived will which desires the *free pleasure* of God. But now it has taken into itself the horrible, *harsh*, hard, *stinging sharpness*. Now, both of these clash together: the *sharp* will eagerly and mightily desires the *fire-pleasure*, and the pleasure desires the *harsh* <note>original: "austere"</note> will. As they enter and feel each other, a *great flash* <note>original: "Flagrat," meaning a sudden, powerful ignition or flash of fire</note> is made, like a flash of lightning, in the same way that fire, or celestial lightning, or an ethereal blaze is ignited in the sky.

26. And in this *flash*, the *fire* is ignited. For the *harsh* dark darkness, which is cold, is dismayed at the light and great gentleness of the *free pleasure*, and becomes in itself a *flash of death*. There, the wrathfulness and cold property retire back into themselves and close themselves up like a death. For in the *flash*, the *dark* mind <margin>m Being afraid or dismayed by the light.</margin> becomes *essential*; it sadly retreats into *itself* as ^m a great fear before the light, or as an *enmity* of the light. This is the true origin of the dark world, namely of the *abyss* into which the devils are thrust, which we call **Hell.**

13. But to answer the reader's desire briefly and fully concerning the *seven properties* of the eternal nature—which create *three principles* or worlds—I will (out of love, for the sake of the simple) once more set down the forms in brief as an "A-B-C" <note>meaning a basic primer or introduction</note> for further consideration and meditation.

#### I. *Form: Astringent; Desire.*

14. Look! The *desire* of the *eternal Word* (which is good) is the beginning of the eternal nature. It is the *congealing* of the eternal "Nothing" into "Somethings." It is the cause of *essences*, as well as of cold and heat; likewise of the water and air, and the *formation* of the powers; it is also a cause of taste and a mother of all *salts* <term>In the alchemy of this period, "salts" represent the principle of stability, solidity, or the physical body of a substance.</term>.

#### II. *Form: Bitter; Compunctive.*

15. The motion of the desire—namely (*viz.* <note>original: "viz."; an abbreviation for the Latin "videlicet," meaning "namely"</note>) the *attraction*—is the second form of nature, a cause of all life and movement, as well as of the *senses* and distinction.

#### III. *Form: Anguish; Perception.*

16. The anguish—namely the *sensibility*—is the third form, a cause of the mind, wherein the senses are moved and acted upon.

We see this in the earth and stones, especially in **metals**, where often in one compaction all seven metals are couched together; yet only one property is principal, which coagulates and captivates all the rest within itself. Always one is more manifest than the rest, according to which property has its powerful predominance in a thing. The like is also to be understood in **vegetables** <note>original: "vegetables"; meaning plants in general</note>, where oftentimes in a herb or piece of wood, there is an astringent, sour, harsh, bitter, anxious, or sulfurous property, as well as a fiery, sweet or luscious, flashy or watery quality.

10. ...and speaks it forth from eternity to eternity. 12. The *Trinity* is first rightly understood in His eternal manifestation, where He manifests Himself through eternal nature, through the fire in the light.

In the dark, wrathful source, He is an angry, zealous *avenger*, in which property the spirits of the dark world consist.

14. The Father is only called a holy God in the Son, that is, in the power of the light in the divine kingdom of joy—namely, in the great *meekness* and love. In the dark nature He is not called God.

15. We must make a distinction: each world has its principle and dominion. Indeed, *all* is from one eternal origin, but it separates itself into a twofold source. We have a similarity to this in fire and light: where the fire is painful and *consuming*, and the light is meek and *giving*; and yet the one would be nothing without the other.

16. The fire receives its origin in *nature*, but the light has its origin from the free *lubet* <term>lubet</term>, namely, from the *powers* of the Deity. The will of God therefore introduces itself into a *fire* so that He might manifest the light and the powers, and introduce them into *essence.*

17. Although I have written here of the forms of nature (meaning the eternal nature), it must not be understood as if the Deity were circumscribed or limited. #### CHAP. VIII.
#### Of the Creation of Angels, and their Dominion.

1. The creation of angels had a beginning, but the powers out of which they are created never had any beginning; rather, they were present during the birth of the Eternal Beginning. This does not mean <margin>Namely, the Powers.</margin> they are the Holy Trinity itself or within the same; instead, they were conceived from the desire for divine manifestation out of the eternal dark, fiery, and light-nature—out of the Manifested Word—and introduced into creaturely forms and shapes.

2. God, who is a Spirit, has through his manifestation introduced himself into distinct spirits. These are the voices of his eternal, fertile harmony in the Manifested Word of his great kingdom of joy. They are God's instruments, in which the Spirit of God creates melody in his kingdom of joy; they are the flames of fire and light, but existing within a living, understanding dominion.

3. For the powers of the Deity are in them in the same way they are in men, as John says in Chapter 1: "the life of men was in the Word." So also the life of the angels was in the Word from eternity; for in Matthew 22:30 it is written: "in the Resurrection they (meaning men) are as the angels of God in Heaven."

4. And just as we understand principal forms in the divine manifestation through eternal nature, so we are also to understand Archangels, or Angelic groups of rulers, with many legions. These are especially arranged in three hierarchies according to the property of the Holy Trinity, and also the three Principles, as cannot be denied.

This is also what happened to Adam when he desired both evil and good; then the free *Lubet* of the holy world’s essence disappeared within his own essence.

13. This was the very death of which God told him: that if he ate of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, he should die the very same day. Thus it was with Lucifer; he died to the holy divine world and arose to the wrathful world of God’s anger.

14. You ask: "Why did God not uphold him and draw him away from the evil inclination?" I ask you, with what? Should He have poured more love and meekness into this fire-source? If so, his majestic light would have been even more manifest in him, the looking-glass of his own knowledge would have been greater, and his own fiery self-will would have become even stronger. I ask you: were not his high light and his own self-knowledge the very cause of his fall?

15. Should He then have drawn him with a rebuke? Was it not his purpose beforehand to rule the magical ground as an <term>Artist</term> <note>In this context, "Artist" refers to a master of the "Art" of spiritual alchemy or the manipulation of the forces of nature.</note>? His aim and endeavor was for the "Art," so that he could play with the center of the transmutation of properties and be and do whatever he alone pleased. Had he not known this, he would have remained an angel in humility.

16. Therefore, the children of darkness and the children of this world are also wiser than the children of light, as the Scripture says. You ask, why? They have the magical root of the origin of essences manifest in them. This was the very desire of Adam; however, the Devil persuaded them that they would be wiser, their eyes would be opened, and they would be like God Himself.

17. This folly caused King Lucifer to aspire, desiring to be an artist and absolute lord like the Creator. The water of meekness would have been good for his fire-will, but he wanted none of it. Hence it is that the children of God must be the most plain, sincere, and simple; as Isaiah prophesied of Christ: *who is so simple as my servant the righteous one, who turns many unto righteousness*—namely, <margin>Or to.</margin> upon the way of humility.

18. All angels live in humility and are resigned to the Spirit of God. They exist in the eternal speaking Word of God like a well-tuned, pure-sounding instrument in the harmony of the kingdom of heaven, of which the Holy Spirit is the chief Master and Ruler.

19. But the Devil has forged for himself a strange "fool’s play," where he can act out his deceptions with his various interludes and disguises. He demeans himself like an apish fool and transforms himself into monstrous, strange, and hideous shapes and figures. **CHAP. 10. Of the Creation of Heaven and 35**

# CHAPTER X.

*Of the Creation of Heaven and the Outward World.*

1. It seems strange and wonderful to *Reason* to consider how God has created the *stars* and the four elements, especially when it contemplates and considers the Earth with its hard stones and very rough, undigested, harsh substance. It sees that there are great stones, rocks, and cliffs created which are in part *useless* and very burdensome to the work of the creatures in this world. Then it thinks: from where might this *compaction* <term>original: "compaction"; the solidifying or hardening of matter into physical form</term> arise in so many forms and properties? For there are various sorts of stones, various metals, and various kinds of earth from which many herbs and trees grow.

2. Now, when it muses and contemplates in this way, it finds nothing except to acknowledge that there must be a hidden power and might which is abyssal <term>bottomless or unfathomable</term> and unsearchable, which has created all things so. And there it gets stuck; it runs to and fro in the creation like a bird that flies up and down in the air. It looks upon all things as an ox looks at a new stall door, and never even considers what it is itself. It seldom reaches so far as to know that man is an image extracted out of this *whole Being*. It runs up and down like a beast void of understanding, which desires only to eat and procreate. When it reaches its highest level, seeking to search out and learn something, it then searches in the outward *fiction* <note>original: "fiction"; here meaning the external appearance, structure, or fashioned shape of the world</note> and artifice of the *stars*, or else in some carved work of outward nature. It will by no means simply and sincerely learn to know its Creator. When it happens that someone attains enough knowledge to teach about Him, it then calls that person a *fool* and a "fantastic" <note>original: "phantaſtick"; in this context, someone driven by delusions, imagination, or groundless whims</note>, and *forbids* them the precious understanding of God, accusing them of sin and reviling them for it.

3. We are such mere animals since the Fall of *Adam* that we do not even once consider that we were created in the image of God and endowed with the right, natural, and genuine *understanding* of both eternal and temporal nature. We should, with great earnestness, mind and think how to regain what we have lost, whereas we still have that very first soul in which the true understanding lies. If we only seriously labored to have that light which we lost shine in us again—which is still offered to us out of Grace.

4. Therefore, *there will be no excuse at the great day of the Lord, when God shall judge the secret and hidden things of mankind*, because we would not learn to know Him and obey His voice, which has knocked daily among us and in us, nor resign ourselves to Him so that our understanding might be opened. And a very severe sentence shall he receive who undertakes to be called *Master*, and

14. And in this impression, or conjunction, the powers—namely the watery and oily properties—were compacted. This Word took away the disobedient child’s *inheritance* <note>original: "Patrimony"</note> and cast him out as a treacherous wretch from his inheritance into an eternal prison, into the house of darkness and anger. There, he had desired to be master over the essence of God’s *Love* and to rule there as a deceiver and enchanter, mixing the holy with the unholy to perform his deceptive feats and proud pranks.

15. And we see very clearly with sharp-sighted eyes that it is so: for there is nothing in this world so evil that it does not have some good in it. The *Good* has its origin in the good or heavenly property, and the *Evil* has its descent from the property of the dark world; for both worlds—light and darkness—exist within each other as one.

**V. Oil.**

22. **F**ifthly, we find in the solidification <note>original: "Compaction"</note> of the metals and stones an Oil which is sweeter than any sugar can be, so far as it may be separated from the other properties. It is the first heavenly, holy essence, which has taken its origin from the free delight <note>original: "Lubet"—a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the divine desire or the "will" of the abyss.</note>. It is pure and transparent; but if the fire-source be severed from it (although it is impossible to wholly separate it, for the bond of the great triumphant joy consists within it), then it is whiter than anything can be in nature. But by reason of the fire, it remains a rosy-red <margin>Or crimson purple-red.</margin>, which the light changes into yellow according to the mixture of red and white, caused by the earthly property and the predominant influence of the Sun.

23. But if the Artist <note>Refers to the alchemist or seeker of spiritual wisdom.</note> can unlock it and free it from the fire of the wrath and other properties, then he has the Pearl of the whole world—understand this as the Tincture <note>original: "Tincture"—in alchemy, a spiritualized substance capable of transforming and perfecting matter.</note>. For Virgin Venus has her cabinet of treasure lying there; it is the Virgin with her fair attire, or crown of pearl.

24. O you earthly man, if only you still had it! Here Lucifer and Adam have negligently lost it! O man! If only you knew what lay here, how you would seek after it! But it belongs only to those whom God has chosen for it. O precious Pearl, how sweet you are in the new birth; how fair and surpassingly excellent is your luster.

**VI. The Living Mercury; Sound.**

25. **S**ixthly, we find in this oily property a sovereign power from the origin of the manifested, powerful Divine Word, which dwells in the heavenly property. In this power, the sound or tone of metals is distinguished, and their growth consists within it. For here it is the holy Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"—representing the life-force, movement, and communication in alchemical thought.</note>. That which in the second form of nature in the darkness is stinging <note>original: "Compunctive"</note>, harsh, rigid, and a poison, is here in the property of the free delight—when the fire in the saltpeter-flash <note>original: "Salnitrall Flagrat"—a term for a sudden burst of divine or natural energy.</note> has divided love and anger—a pleasant, merry Mercury, in which the joyfulness of the creature consists.

26. And here, you philosophers, lies the effective virtue and powerful operation of your noble stone; here it is called Tincture. This operation can "tincture" (transform) the disappeared water in the Moon <note>original: "Luna"—in alchemy, silver.</note>. For here your Jupiter <note>Alchemical tin.</note> is a prince, and the Sun <note>original: "Sol"—in alchemy, gold.</note> is a king, and Virgin Venus <note>Alchemical copper.</note> is the king's sweetest spouse. But Mars <note>Alchemical iron.</note> must first lay down his scepter; also the Devil must first go into hell, for Christ must bind him and tincture simple Luna (which the Devil has defiled) with the oil of His heavenly blood, so that the anger may be changed into joy. Thus the Artist's art is born, understood here by the children of the Mystery.

**VII. Essence, Body.**

27. **S**eventhly, we find in the separation of the solidification of the metals a white crystalline water; that is, the heavenly water.

# Chapter 10: Of the Creation of Heaven and Earth <meta>This page continues the discussion of the divine process of creation, focusing on how spiritual forces solidify into the material world.</meta> 41

34. The *Star* <note>original: *Astrum*</note> <margin>Or constellation</margin> represents the Spirit, and the Earth represents the Body. Before the Creation, everything existed within each other in the eternal generation <note>The "eternal generation" refers to the continuous process by which the divine source brings all things into being</note>, but without any solidification <note>original: *Coagulation*</note> or creaturely form. Instead, it was like a powerful, wrestling play of love without any such material substance.

35. But it was ignited by the motion of the Word—namely, the *Word: "Let it be"* <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*</note>. With that, a fire was lit in the spiritual explosion <note>original: *Sal-nitrall Flagrat*; a term describing the sudden flash of divine energy that brings nature into being</note>. Each property divided itself within itself and was gathered together by the awakened, contractive power (namely, the first form of nature, which is called the *Fiat*). Thus, each property became solidified in its own property: the refined in its property and the dense in its property. All this happened according to the various degrees, just as the eternal generation of nature spreads itself from unity into an infinite multiplicity.

36. Good and evil are revealed in the *Star* <note>original: *Astrum*</note> <margin>Or constellation</margin>. For both the wrathful, fiery power of eternal nature and the power of the holy, spiritual world are revealed in the stars as an essential breathing out <note>original: *spiration*</note>. Therefore, there are many dark stars that we cannot see, and many bright stars that we can see.

37. We see a likeness of this in the matter of the Earth, which is so diverse and from which many kinds of fruit grow, according to the properties of the higher spheres. The Earth is the same way, being the densest substance where the perishable <note>original: *mortall*</note> water has solidified.

38. The Earth solidified in the *seventh form of nature*, namely, in the Essence. For it is that same Essence which the other six properties create through their desire. It primarily consists of seven properties, as mentioned above. However, the unfolding or various explanations of these properties are achieved in the spiritual fire <note>original: *Salnitrall fire*</note>, where each property again unfolds itself into seven. This is where the infinite possibility <margin>Or potency</margin> arises, allowing one thing to be made into another thing which it was not in the beginning.

39. The Being of all beings is only a magical birth, coming out of the One into infinity. The *One* is God; the infinite is time and eternity, a manifestation of the *One*. In this manifestation, every thing may be transformed from one into many, and again from many back into one.

40. Fire is the chief master craftsman in this process. It pushes a small sprout out of the earth with a little power and develops it into a great tree with many boughs, branches, and fruits. Then, it consumes it again and reduces it back to one thing—namely, to ashes and earth, from which it first came. In the same way, all things of this world enter again into the *One* from which they originated.

41. The essence of this world may be easily investigated, but the *center* or point of motion will remain dark to human reason unless there is another light within it. Reason assumes it has captured this center within its circle <margin>Or mathematically describe and demonstrate it</margin> and can measure it, but it does not possess it in its understanding.

42. When we consider the hierarchy and the kingly dominion in all the three principles <note>The "Three Principles" are the core of Boehme's philosophy: the dark world of fire/will, the light world of love/spirit, and the outer world of nature</note> in this world, we see how far the *Word: "Let it be"* <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*</note> extended itself to the creation of the outward world, with its stars and elements. Then we have the foundation of the *Point* <note>original: *Punctum*</note> <margin>Central fire or radical heat; the point of motion, the virtue of the light</margin> and the Royal Throne, of which the whole creation is but a member.

47. By the two words (*Heaven and Earth*) we understand the whole ground of the creation; for the understanding is crouched in the language of nature in those two words. For by the word (*Heaven* <note>original: "Himmell"</note>) is understood the "spiration" <note>breathing forth</note> of the *Verbum Fiat* <note>original Latin: the "Word [that says] Let there be," the creative command from Genesis</note>, which created that essence (wherein Lucifer was enthroned) with the creative word out of itself; that is, out of the spiritual holy world, into a time or beginning. And by the word (*Earth* <note>original: "Erde"</note>) is understood the wrath in the essence; meaning that the essence was amassed in the wrath and reduced out of the properties of the dark sulfur, mercury, and salt <note>In the alchemical tradition, these "Three Principles" represent the fundamental components of all matter: soul, spirit, and body</note>—namely, out of the powers of the origin of nature—and introduced into a **compaction** or coagulation.

48. This coagulation is the syllable (*Er*); the other syllable (*de* or *den*) is the element. For the earth is not the element, but the [element is] the moving—namely the power—from which it was coagulated. This is that **element** which is spiritual and takes its true origin in the fire, where nature (which is a senseless life) dies in the fire. From which **dying**, or mortification then, there proceeds forth a **living** motion; and from that which is mortified [in the fire] comes a dead matter, namely earth, and a dead water, and also a deadly fire and venomous air, which makes a dying **source** in the earthly bodies.

49. When nature was ignited, the Element unfolded [and displayed] itself into four properties, which yet in itself is only one. The real Element dwells in the essence which is neutralized <note>original: "mortified"; in this context, it refers to the subduing of the harsh qualities of fire to create a stable essence</note> in the fire; otherwise, the Earth could bring forth no fruit. Those which are now called the four elements are not the true elements, but only properties of the true Element. The Element is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor moist; it is the motion or life of the inward heaven, namely <note>original: "viz."</note> the true angelic life as it relates to the creature. It is the first divine manifestation out of the fire, through nature; when the properties of the eternal nature work within it, it is called Paradise.

50. By the word * Heaven <note>original: * Himmel</note> <margin>* Heaven</margin> it is understood how the water—namely, the coarseness in the mortal part—was solidified and separated from the holy crystalline water, which is spiritual. With this material part, time began, as an essence expressed [or breathed out] from the spiritual water.

51. The spiritual water is living, and the breathed-out water is lifeless, senseless, void of understanding, and is dead in reference to the living water, of which Moses says God separated it from the water above the firmament.

52. The firmament is another principle—namely, another beginning [or inception] of motion. The water above the firmament is the spiritual water in which the Spirit of God rules and works; for Moses also says, "the Spirit of God moved upon the water." For the spiritual Element moves within the four elements, and in the spiritual Element the Spirit of God moves on the spiritual water; they are mutually within each other.

53. The heaven where God dwells is the holy Element; and the firmament, or gulf between God and the four elements, is death. For the inward heaven has another birth (that is, another life) than the external elementary life has. Indeed, they are within one another, but the one does not grasp the other, just as tin and silver never mix properly together; for each is from a different <note>original: "sundry"</note> principle. Although they resemble each other and have a very near affinity to each other, they are like the inward and outward water to one another. In this way, they are also to be understood: for the inward and outward Venus <note>In alchemy and Boehme’s philosophy, Venus often represents the desire or the "sweet" quality of nature</note> are step-sisters; they come indeed from one father, but they have two mothers. One of them is a virgin, and the other is deflowered; therefore, they are separated until the judgment of God, who will purge away her reproach and shame through the fire.

54. Moses writes that God created the heaven out of the midst of the waters; this is very correct. The * Starry Heaven <note>original: "Astrum"</note> <margin>* Understand by the word "Astrum" (Starry Heaven) the whole starry sky with all its powers, properties, influences, and constellations, both internal and external.</margin> is an external water-spirit, namely the powers of the outward water; and the material water is the body in which the powers work. Now the fiery, airy, and also earthly essence <note>original: "Source"</note> is in the Starry Heaven; the same is also in the material water. The superior [Starry Heaven] is the life and dominion of the inferior; it ignites the inferior, by which the inferior acts, moves, and works. The inferior is the body or wife of the superior; indeed, the superior is hidden <note>original: "coucht"</note> in the inferior, but as something weak and powerless.

**CHAP. XI.**
***Of the Mystery of the Creation.***

1. The *reason* of the outward man <note>The "outward man" refers to the physical, earthly self as opposed to the internal spiritual soul.</note> says: why is it that God has not revealed the creation of the world to man? Why have *Moses* and the children of God written so little of it, seeing it is the greatest and most principal work, on which the *main thing* depends?
2. Yes! Dear *Reason*, look into your own heart <note>original: "smell into thy own bosom"; a vivid metaphor for self-examination.</note>; what does it *savor* of? Contemplate your own *mind*; what does it long for? Likely, it longs for the cunning delusions of the *Devil*. If he had not known this foundation, it is very likely he would still be an *angel*; had he not seen the *magical* birth in his high light, then he would not have desired to be a selfish lord and maker in the *essence.*
3. Why does God hide his children—who now receive the spirit of knowledge with the *Cross*—and cast them into tribulation and the mire of vanity? Certainly, it is *therefore* so that they might play the tune of *have mercy* <note>original: *miserere*; Latin for "have mercy," referencing Psalm 51, a prayer of repentance</note> and continue in *humility*, and not play in this life with the light of nature. Otherwise, if they should spy and apprehend <margin>Text, Time.</margin> what the *divine magic* <note>Boehme uses "Magic" to describe the creative power of the divine will.</note> is, then they might also desire to imitate the *Devil*, as *Lucifer* did. For this cause, it is hidden from them; and neither *Moses* nor any other dare write more clearly of it, until the beginning of the *creation* sees the end of the world within itself—and then it must stand open.
4. And therefore let no one blame us, for the time has come about: *Moses* puts away the veil from his eyes, which he hung before his face when he spoke with *Israel* after the Lord had spoken with him. *Moses* desired to see it when he said, *Lord, if I have found grace in your sight, let me see your face*; but the Lord would not, and said, *you shall see my back; for no one can see my face.*
5. Now the eye of God was in *Moses* and in the *saints*; they saw and spoke in the spirit of God, and yet they did not have the thorough vision of the *spiritual* birth in them, except at certain times only. When God would work wonders, as he did through *Moses* when he performed the wonders in *Egypt*, then the *divine magic* was open to him in the same manner as it was in the *creation.*
6. And this was the very fall of *Lucifer*: that he wanted to be a god of nature and live in the *transmutation* <note>original: *transmutation*; the alchemical process of changing one substance into another; here, Lucifer's attempt to seize the power of creation</note>; and this was the very idolatry of the—

**CHAPTER 12.**
*Of the Six Days' Works of the Creation.*

1. That God created heaven and earth and all things in six days, as Moses says, is the greatest mystery, and it is completely hidden from external reason <note>original: "externall Reaſon"; human logic based only on physical observation</note>. There is neither night, morning, nor evening in the "Deep" above the moon; instead, there has been one continuous day from the beginning of the outward world until its end.

2. And although the Creation was finished over the length of six days, these "days' works" have a much more subtle and profound <note>original: "abstruce"</note> meaning. For the "Seven Properties" <note>Boehme's system of seven qualities or "source-spirits" of existence</note> are also understood through them. Six of these belong to the active domain of good and evil, and the seventh (namely, the Essence) is the "rest" in which the other properties reside, which God has expressed and made visible.

3. In the domain of the planetary spheres <note>original: "Planetick Orbe"</note>, we have a symbol of how the six properties of active life (which rest in the seventh) introduced and manifested themselves over six days. They came out of the inward spiritual world and into an external, visible world made of the four elements. For the

Likewise, there is an *Astrum* in the manifest heavenly world, and also an *Astrum* in the dark, hellish world. <margin>Or constellations.</margin> These *Astrums* are really only one single *Astrum*, but they are separated into distinct degrees and <term>Principles</term> <note>The basic components or "realms" of existence in Boehme's philosophy</note>. What is open and manifest in form in the outward world is the same as what is manifest in power in the spiritual world, though not in outward shapes.

14. And we understand that on the fourth day, the Word "Let there be" <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*</note> moved the fourth property of nature—the <term>fifth essence</term> <note>The "quintessence," a pure substance thought to be the basis of the physical world</note>—and opened it out of the sulfurous property, from the fire-flash <note>original: *flagrat*; a sudden ignition or outburst</note> (the third property). Thus, an *Astrum* became manifest in the air, which are the visible stars; and an *Astrum* in the fire, which is the rational life of all creatures; and an *Astrum* in the water, which is the vegetative life; and an *Astrum* in the earth, which is the wrathful, earthly life.

15. The fiery *Astrum* gives the soul, and the airy gives the spirit. The watery provides the mansion for the soul and spirit—the blood—where the <term>tincture</term> <note>The fundamental essence or vitalizing quality</note> of the fire and light lives. Finally, the earthly *Astrum* gives the flesh. Each of the four *Astrums* gives a spirit and a body according to its own property. God has joined them together so that one might be manifest in the other, and they might jointly be one body. Just as all four elements are only one element, they divide themselves into four properties according to the center of nature.

16. These four <margin>constellations</margin> *Astrums* produce from themselves their "officer"—the outward nature—which is the soul of the outward world, acting as a constantly enduring mind. Within this lies omnipotence, as a manifest great mystery. In this "officer," God has awakened and raised a King—or, to use a comparison, a "nature-god"—with six counselors who are his assistants. This is the Sun <note>original: *Sol*</note> along with the six other planetary stars. These were spoken into existence from the seven properties out of the place of the Sun; in that speaking, they were introduced into a rolling sphere according to the property of eternal generation in the center of nature. This was opened in seven degrees out of the birth, where the sixth degree of motion in the light of nature (from the inward spiritual fire and light-world) was the Sun. The Sun receives its luster from the tincture of the inward fire and light-world; it stands as an open point <note>original: *Punctum*</note> to the fire-world.

First came Venus, which is the water-source out of the gentleness that comes from the "killing" <note>original: *mortification*; here meaning the tempering or transformation of raw energy</note> of the fire. Every *being* <note>original Latin: "Ens"</note> brings forth a likeness of itself.

They live in those elements and take their food and nourishment from them. For the *Divine Command* <note>original Latin: "Fiat"; "Let it be"</note> extracted them out of the earth's property and gathered them in the fifth manifestation of essence as a "sulfur" <note>In the "alchemy of the soul," sulfur represents the combustible, active, or soul-like quality of a substance.</note> of the *fifth being*, upon which the other four depend.

11. The *birds* were created in the sulfur of the air; therefore, they fly in their "mother" element. Likewise, the *fish* were created in the sulfur of the water, and the *worms* in the sulfur of the earth. Thus, every thing lives in the "mother" from which it was originally taken, and the opposite environment is its death.

Whatever potential eternity contains, and whatever kind of spiritual activity exists in the *being* <note>original Latin: "Ens"</note> of the inward spiritual world, has come forth accordingly into a created existence—made of good and evil—into time, through *Divine Motion.*

He was not made a creature in this principle, and he has no life in it, except only...

6. Then God said: *Let us make man as an image according to our likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.* <note>Genesis 1:26</note> This "clay" <term>original: *Limus*</term> out of which God created the body of man is a refined extract <note>original: *Massa*</note> of all essences, representing both the properties of the stars and the four elements. It was formed through the creative Word <note>original: *Fiat*</note>—the same Word that created the entire world—into a spiritual-physical source <term>original: *Matrix*</term> or mass.

7. This clay <note>original: *Limus*</note> was an extract of all that the universe is, both in its spiritual and material parts. It originated from the divine conception <term>original: *Enthymeris*</term> of the creative Word <note>original: *Verbum*</note>, as a physical manifestation of the divine blueprint <term>original: *Idea*</term> which existed in the wisdom of God from eternity.

8. Thus, the human body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> is a manifestation of the "Third Principle"—the visible world. It is the habitation of the internal, spiritual image that was formed according to the divine likeness.

9. For this image was already present in the "Divine Mystery" <note>the *Mysterium Magnum*, or the hidden potential within God</note> before the beginning of time. In the creation, God introduced this spiritual image into a physical essence, forming a being that could exist within the material realm.

10. Moses says, *In the image of God he created him.* This distinction is vital: man was not just made *like* God in a general sense, but was created specifically *into* the divine image that existed eternally in God's wisdom.

11. To understand the creation of the body, we must see that it was not made of simple dirt, but of a concentrated mass <note>original: *Massa*</note> of all the powers of the stars and the elements. All the properties of the macrocosm <note>the great world or universe</note> were compressed into this microcosm <note>the "little world," which is man</note> through the power of the creative Word <note>original: *Fiat*</note>.

12. As Moses rightly says: *God created man [IN] his image, [TO] the image of God.* <note>Boehme is analyzing the specific prepositions used in the Latin or German versions of Genesis</note>. The word "IN" signifies that man was known by the Spirit of God in his very essence from eternity, residing within the mystery of divine wisdom as a constellation of magical power. Into this eternal knowledge, God introduced a tangible substance <note>original: *Essence*</note> and created that substance *to* or *as* the physical image of that eternal, magical blueprint of God.

Thus each power has a *corporeal* property in it, and the inward powers of the spiritual property are to be understood with the inward body in the same way.
