CHAPTER 16. On the difference of the [space] 67

## CHAPTER XVI.
*On the difference between the Heavenly and Earthly Man.*

1. When we consider the *Image of God* that God created in Paradise for eternal, incorruptible life, we cannot say that the gross, fleshy image—the crude quality of earthliness—is the Image of God which can possess the holy world. For it is not of the same essence and <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens," Latin for "being" or "essence"</note>; as Christ also says in John 6: *The Spirit is life; the flesh profits nothing.* Also: *flesh and blood shall not inherit the Kingdom of Heaven.* And yet, truly, the true body is hidden within this beastly, gross quality, just as gold is found within the ore.

2. Everything earthly about a person is beastly and corruptible, and is not the true man. Although God created an external body for Man out of the <term>limus</term> <note>original: "limus," Latin for "mud" or "clay," referring to the dust of the ground in Genesis</note> of the earth, we should not think of it as it is now. For the true human body, according to the *inward world*, is a spiritual *Sulfur*, a spiritual *Mercury*, and a spiritual *Salt*. <note>Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt were the "Three Primes" of alchemy, representing the soul, spirit, and physical matter.</note> Every quality of the soul has a corporeal or essential quality attached to it.

3. God created such a body as the soul was in its essence—namely, in the breathed-out Word of understanding—and breathed the soul into it for *understanding*. Furthermore, the outward "sulfurous" body is by no means the "Gross Beast" which passes away and never returns. The true, real body, which is *hidden* in that grossness, is a spiritual body compared to the *grossness*. It was indeed created in flesh and blood, but in a fixed, steadfast [incorruptible flesh and blood].

4. Because of the lust and imagination of *Adam*, the grossness became manifest. The true outward body is a quality of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt; a pure, essential *power* according to the nature of the soul. The light shone through all the qualities and created an equal <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature," meaning a perfect balance or mixture of elements</note> among them. All the qualities gave their desire to the light—namely, into the revealed sweetness of God, which penetrated all the qualities. In this penetration, they were all <term>tinctured</term> <note>original: "Tinctured," meaning infused or dyed with a spiritual quality</note> with *Sweet Love*, so that there was nothing but pure, pleasing flavor, love-desire, and delight between them.

7. Thus the inward man held the outward captive within itself and penetrated it, just as fire heats iron through until it seems as if it were all fire. But when the fire goes out, then the dark, *black* <note>original: "swart"</note> iron is revealed.

Just as time is a play <margin>before</margin> God, so also the outward life of man was a play for the *inward* holy man, who was the true image of God.

9. The outward spirit and body were to the inward like a *wonder* of *divine manifestation* according to the fire-dark and light worlds—a mirror of the great *omnipotence* and *omniscience* of God. The inward was given to the outward as a ruler and guide.

No heat or cold bothered him. Just as a *tincture* penetrates a body and protects it from sickness, and as the warmth of the *sun* defends the body from cold, so the highest *tincture* of fire and light—the holy power of the inward spiritual body—penetrated the outward body of flesh and blood. It took every outward elemental property, as well as the materials <note>original: "limms," here referring to the constituent parts or elements</note> of the earth, under its protection.

As gold endures in the fire, and as a *tincture* penetrates all things and yields to nothing, so man was not subject to anything except God alone. God dwelt within him and was *revealed* in him with the power of the holy essence. This was an image and likeness of God, in whom the Spirit of God lived.

13. *Reason* will misunderstand us and say that I speak of two different men, but I say no! I speak of only one man, who is a *likeness* of God—that is, according to the revealed God, according to the expressed, formed word of *divine* power and divine understanding.

**CHAPTER XVII.**
**Of Paradise.**

1. Moses says that when God had made man, He planted a garden in Eden, and there He put man to till and keep it. He caused all manner of fruits to grow that were pleasant to the sight and good for food; He also planted the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil in the midst of it.

2. Here lies the veil before the face of Moses <note>A reference to Exodus 34:29-35, where Moses veiled his face because it shone too brightly for the Israelites to look upon; Boehme uses this as a metaphor for spiritual truths hidden from the worldly mind</note>. Because he had a bright, shining face, sinful Israel could not look him in the eye; for the man of vanity is not worthy to know what Paradise is. Although it is given to us to know it according to our "hidden man" <note>The spiritual or inner self</note>, yet by this description, we shall remain as if mute to the "Beast" <note>The animalistic, earthly nature of man</note>, though we will be sufficiently understood by our fellow scholars.

3. The Garden of Eden was a place upon the earth where man was tempted; and Paradise was in heaven, and yet it was also in the Garden of Eden. For just as Adam—before his Eve [was made out of him] and before his sleep—was in heaven as to his inward man, and upon the earth as to his outward man; and just as the inward holy man penetrated the outward, as a fire heats through a piece of iron; so also the heavenly power out of the Pure Element <note>In Boehme's thought, the "Pure Element" is the spiritual substance of the heavenly world, distinct from the four earthly elements</note> penetrated the four elements and sprang forth through the earth. It bore fruits which were both heavenly and earthly, and were tempered <gloss>sweetly balanced</gloss> by divine power. The "vanity" in the fruit was held as if swallowed up, just as the day hides the night and holds it captive within itself, so that the night is neither known nor manifest.

4. Paradise was nothing else but the property of the seventh day. The heavenly essentiality <term>essentiality: substantial spiritual reality</term> of the second principle <note>The "second principle" refers to the realm of Light or the Son in Boehme’s cosmology</note> is couched or shut up in the earth. The curse of God has hidden it. In the beginning of the world, it budded through the earthly substance, just as eternity is within time, and divine power is through all things; and yet it is neither comprehended nor understood by any earthly thing in its own "selfhood" <note>The ego or state of being separated from God</note>.

5. But in Paradise, the essence of the divine world penetrated the essence of time, just as the sun penetrates the fruit upon a tree and effectively works it into a pleasantness, so that it is lovely to look upon and good to eat. We are to understand the Garden in Eden in the same way.

16. Reason asks: Why did God allow this tree to grow if man was not supposed to eat from it? Did He not bring it forth for the fall of man? And must it not necessarily be the cause of man’s destruction? This is the very thing about which the "high schools" <note>Referring to academic theologians and universities.</note> argue without understanding. They try to find and grasp the *inward* through the *outward*, but it remains hidden and dead to them because they do not understand what Man is.

17. Man was created out of all *three principles* and was placed within the properties of the inward and outward world in equal number, weight, and measure. None of the principles exceeded the others; there was a perfect harmony. The divine light balanced <note>original: "temperized"</note> all the properties so that there was a mutual *melody* and play of unanimous love between them.

18. The fiery, dark world rejoiced in the holy light-world, and the light-world rejoiced in the outward world as its manifestation. In turn, the outward world enjoyed both inward worlds as its life. There was nothing but a *pleasing, harmonious* will, pleasure, and sweet delight between them. The *Mercury*—that is <note>original: "viz."</note>, the sounding, hearing, and feeling life, which is the manifestation of the divine Word in the *Let it be done* <note>original: "Fiat"</note>—mutually penetrated all essences in a very joyful way.

26. ...into the fiery Mystery, towards the darkness from which the fire arises; and so the magical *Astrum* <note>original: "Astrum," referring here to a celestial or spiritual influence or "star"</note> of the Grand Mystery of the dark world seized him. 29. Thus we are to know that his fall happened because of his own *creaturely nature*. For had he not turned away his creaturely desire from *divine meekness* and love in pride and stubborn will—seeking to rule in the *Matrix* of the Pregnatress <note>original: "Matrix of the Pregnatress," a term for the generative or birthing power of nature</note> which treated him like an actor—he would have remained an angel. Had he continued under God's love-spirit and will, then his anger-spirit and will would not have captivated him.

30. But seeing as he has freely and willingly broken himself off from God's love-will, he now has God's anger-will within him. In this, he must be a manifestor and worker of the dark world's property, for *it* also desired to be creaturely. Here the dark world has a true *captive* who can skillfully act in "ape-like mockery" <note>original: "Apes-sport," meaning a distorted or foolish imitation of divine creativity</note>. Now, as the *dark world* is in its property and its desire, such also is its *Hierarch* or creaturely prince.

31. And here it is very necessary for us to know correctly how man came to fall. Man was created in the stead and place of the *cast-out Lucifer*—understand this as the *inward spiritual man*. He was created in the same heaven according to the inward human soul, and was meant to possess the rank which *Lucifer* had lost; and from this, the *Devil’s envy* against man has arisen.

32. It comes to purge it through the fire, and to introduce His highest love into it, and to overcome the wrath (which *Lucifer* had awakened) with love, and change it again into divine joy—that is, into a *holy heaven* <margin>^u Or unto which end the last judgment is appointed.</margin>—in which place the *Last Judgment* stands. And this is what Saint *Paul* says: *Man was chosen* [or elected] *in Christ Jesus before the foundation of the world was laid.*

For God saw very well, according to the nature of his wrath, that man would fall; but he would bring him back again through and in the name of Jesus, through corruptible death, into the royal kingdom from which Lucifer had fallen. In Lucifer's place, the man Christ—God and man in one person—should sit as a hierarch <note>original: "Hierarck"; a high-ranking religious leader</note>, high priest, or the great prince of men, in the name and power of Jesus out of JEHOVAH.

34. Therefore, we are here to rightly consider the fall of man: how he stood in Paradise and was tempted, and what Paradise was. Man stood in three principles <note>In the theology of Jacob Boehme, these are the three realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light holy-world, and the outer visible world</note>, which indeed stood within man himself—namely, in body and soul—in equal accord and harmony, but not outside of him. For the dark world has a different desire than the light world. Now the image of God stood between three principles; all three set their desire upon this image. Each wanted to be manifest in Adam and have him under their dominion as a ruler, and to manifest their wonders through him.

35. But he—namely, the man—should have directed <note>original: "introduced"</note> his desire only into the sixth property of the divine manifestation, in which he was created as an image of God. He should have been wholly resigned to God. He should only live in the manifested Divine Word, in obedience to God, and not enter into his own will, but direct his desire into God's will—namely, into the sixth property. Thus, the manifested Word of God might be his will, knowing, and doing, just as the holy angels live and rejoice only in the divine will, and make melody in the Holy Ghost, as he opens and manifests himself in them according to divine wisdom. In this way, they live, will, and act with a childlike mind and will.

36. Paradise, or the garden in Eden, did indeed stand with its properties in equal harmony as to man. But the properties were in themselves an awakened hunger, each within itself, which truly the divine light introduced back into a balance <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect proportion or harmony between conflicting elements</note>. But the Devil opposed man in his ignited <note>original: "Enkindled"</note> envy and inserted <note>original: "insinuated"</note> his poisonous imagination into human nature <note>original: "property"</note>. He ignited the human properties in the center, in the first principle of the soul’s nature, where the soul stands in the same essence and being as the angels and devils.

37. From this, Adam's imagination and earnest hunger arose: that he would eat of evil and good and live in his own will. That is, his will departed out of the equal harmony into the multiplicity of the properties; for he wanted to prove, feel, taste, hear, smell, and see them. As the Devil also persuaded them through the serpent, they should be as God, and their eyes should be opened to the properties. This also happened to them in the fall: they knew, tasted, saw, and felt evil and good. From this arose sickness, disease, pains, and corruption—or the dissolution of this carcass.

For it was because of *Adam*, while he was still in Paradise, when he lusted after vanity and brought his imagination into the earth—that is, into that essence from which the clay <note>original: *limus* (Latin for mud or clay)</note> of the outward body was extracted. Reason asks: why did God allow this to happen? *Christ said, "If you had faith as a grain of mustard seed, and should say to this mountain, 'be cast into the sea,' it would be done."* I pray you, was not the soul's spirit sprung forth out of the great divine omnipotence, out of the center of the eternal spiritual nature from which all beings were created? Should it not then be powerful?

42. He was a spark of fire from God's *might*, but when he was formed into a creaturely being, he withdrew into *self-centered* lust and broke himself off from the *Universal Being*. He entered into a state of self-importance, and so he worked his own *destruction*; and this he would have kept, if God's love had not *redeemed* him.

43. The soul's power was so *potent* before the vanity entered that it was not subject to anything; and it is still powerful, if its understanding were not taken away from it. It can, by *magic* <note>In this context, "magic" refers to the spiritual power of the will to act upon nature.</note>, alter all things that exist in the essence of the outward world and introduce them into another essence. But the *vanity* in the dominion of the outer air has brought a darkness into it, so that it does not know itself. The curse of God has cast the defiled child into the dirt, so that it must pray for a cleansing <note>original: *Laver*—a basin used for ritual washing or baptism</note>; it must be its *own enemy* during this lifetime so that it may learn to be humble, remain in the divine harmony, and not become a devil.

### Of the Origin of Actual Sin, and of the * Awakening of God's Anger in the Human Property.

1. The Scripture says, "God has made all things by his word, and without the same, nothing was made which is made" (John 1). Out of his Expressed Word (which was essential in the "Word of Creation" <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*</note>), all things came forth into forms: first into an essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> or the desire of a property, and out of that same property into a solidification <note>original: "compaction"</note> of sulfur, mercury, and salt <note>In alchemy, these three substances—the *Tria Prima*—were believed to be the base components of all matter.</note> as into a formed nature. Out of that same essence within the formed nature, the word becomes a creaturely life. It brings itself forth out of the solidification of sulfur, mercury, and salt, and out of the body <margin>^d Or into a body.</margin>; that is, it manifests itself in a plain, visible being. This is the purpose for which God has created nature and the creature.

2. Thus, each creature has a center for its own re-expression or breathing forth of the formed word *within itself*. This applies to both eternal and temporary creatures, the irrational animals as well as man. For the first essence was spoken forth out of God's breath through Wisdom, out of the center toward the fire and light, then taken into the "Let it be" <note>original: *Fiat*</note> and brought into a solid form.

3. This same essence is from ^e Eternity <margin>^e Or eternal being.</margin>, but the solidification of the four elements is from *Time*. Thus, an eternal essence lies hidden in everything within Time—in all things, whether living or without life, in elements and creatures, in things that grow <note>original: "vegetative"</note> and things that do not. The first essence is in every thing. The form of the physical body (which arose from time) was spoken forth out of the being of the spiritual worlds as an eternal essence out of the Eternal-Speaking Word, through Wisdom into a time—namely <note>original: *viz.*</note> into a formed essence according to the spiritual essence. This essence cannot be destroyed by any element or thing whatsoever.

re-expressing: for man carries the Word which created Heaven and Earth in his essence <note>original: *Ens*; here meaning the fundamental being or spiritual substance of a person</note>, for that same word is brought into substance.

37. Now God has inspired into man’s essence—namely, into the formed, solidified Word—the living soul: that is, the original [understanding] <margin>or understanding</margin> out of all three principles, as a spirit of the formed Word. This understanding now has the power and might to re-conceive and to generate again a formal *voice* in the essence, namely, in the formed, solidified Word.

38. But since the serpent's craft—namely, the Devil's introduced desire—became manifest in the essence of *Adam* and *Eve* (that is, in their solidified and formed Word), the free will now draws forth pure adder’s poison and death from this serpent’s essence and forms its own word within it. This continues unless the holy essence or "seed of the woman" is awakened again in the reborn love of God in Christ. If it is, then the free will may conceive within this same holy essence and "bruise the head" of the *serpent’s* and Devil’s essence in the anger of God. That is, it rejects and abhors the evil will, which desires to take shape <note>original: *Idea*; to take form or imagine</note> and imprint itself from the serpent’s essence in the formation of words. It crushes that evil in the will of the *thoughts* with the essence of the woman—namely, of Christ—and regards it as the Devil’s mire and dirt. In the children of God, this is a continual combat and strife between the essence of the serpent in the flesh and the regenerated essence of the heavenly part.

39. Know this as well: every thought which is formed in the *will*, so that a man consents to lies or anything else that is false, or if his will has conceived <insert>and contrived</insert> anything that is unjust and he brings that contrivance into his desire so that he would very willingly do it or express it in the false, evil-formed word if he could or knew how, and yet must leave it alone for fear or shame—this is all sin. For the will has formed itself in the serpent's essence.

40. But understand this well: if a good will forms itself <margin>or forms itself</margin> in a good essence, and yet the evil desire clings to it and wants to poison the good, if then (I say) the good, conceived will overcomes the evil and casts it out so that the evil cannot also be formed or received into the solidification or substance, it is no sin. And though the evil desire which clings to the good is *sin*, yet if the good will does not join with it and bring it into *substance*, but rejects it out of the good will as an evil, then the sinful desire cannot come into *existence* <note>original: *Essence*</note>, and the good will has not performed any evil by this, provided it has not consented to the craft of the serpent.

41. Every sin is born of the foreign essence. If the free will departs from the essence in which God created it, then the sin which is conceived in the will through false desire and brought to existence in the essence of the will (so that a man would gladly do wickedly or unjustly if he could only bring his intent to pass) is also great in the sight of God. But if it proceeds so far as to hurt and injure anyone by word or deed, then the sin is double. For it is formed in its own essence and forms itself also in that into which it introduces the false word, so far as the false word in its speaking finds a place of rest to work <insert>and bring forth its evil fruit</insert>.

42. And therefore the holy word shall judge the false; as also at the end...

Understand that the word has imprinted and formed itself within the creation, both in its *holiness* <margin>f Or out of.</margin> and also in the *anger* <insert>f</insert>, and also in the outward world. For the <term>clay</term><note>original: "limus," referring to the dust or mud of the earth from which Adam was formed</note> of the earth, or the earth itself, was gathered and compacted through the word. So the formed *Word*, which took its beginning in the divine desire—namely, in the <term>command of creation</term><note>original: "Fiat," Latin for "let it be done"</note>—is an exhalation breathed out from the Spirit of God, out of both love and anger. Therefore, it is both evil and good, but the evil was *hidden* and, as it were, wholly swallowed up in the light, just as the night is swallowed by the day.

46. But the sinful desire in Lucifer and Adam has awakened the anger, so that it has become *essentially* manifest. Now the gates of the formed *Word*, both in love and anger, stand open in the earth, and also in the <term>clay</term> of the earth—namely, in man—and also in the free will of man. Whatever he now forms and gathers in his *free will*, that is what he has made, be it either evil or good.

47. But now the evil shall be separated from the good in the judgment of God. In whichever part [either of the evil or good] the human *understanding*—namely, the soul—shall be found, it must enter into it with everything it has done, as if into its own self-made habitation. Therefore Christ says, *their works shall follow them* and be purged (or tested) by the fire. Also at the end, when the books of the <term>essence</term> shall be opened, they shall be judged according to *their works*. For the work, be it evil or good, embraces the soul, unless the soul departs completely from the evil and destroys it again by reconciliation with his *offended* and wronged brother, and drowns the substance in the blood and death of Christ; otherwise, there is no remedy.

...should reflect and ponder within themselves before they intend (or conceive in the will) to do anything; and by no means consent to any false backbiting or approve of it, neither privately nor openly.
   49. For all forged tales and sharp taunts proceed from the *serpent’s essence* <note>original: *Ens*, a philosophical term meaning "being" or "essence"</note>; all cursing, swearing, and stinging insults proceed from the *serpent’s essence*. Indeed, even if they are said in *jest*, the *serpent’s essence* has attached itself through them to what is good and combined them with the spoken word. Therefore, *Christ says: "Do not swear at all; let your* <margin>Note.</margin> *speech be 'yes, yes' and 'no, no'; for whatever is more than these comes from evil"*—that is, it is born of the serpent's essence.
   50. All those who curse and swear have introduced their free will—namely, the poor soul—into the vanity of the *serpent’s essence*. They form their curses and oaths along with all their lewd, wanton talk, which is crafted in the *serpent’s essence*, and they sow into God's anger. On the contrary, all of God's children, who are truly earnest, form their words in the holy *essence*—especially in *prayer*. When the free will of the soul gathers or conceives itself in the holy *essence* (*which is made accessible through Christ's humanity*), then it forms the true, essential word of God within itself, so that it becomes a *substance* <note>Meaning it takes on a spiritual reality or "body".</note>.
   51. Therefore, *Saint Paul says: "The Spirit of God mightily intercedes for us in the sight of God as it pleases Him."* For the Spirit of God is formed in the desire for the holy Word; He is grasped (or apprehended), and this grasping or receiving is what Christ meant when He said *He would give us His flesh for food and His blood for drink.*
   52. The soul's will takes hold of *Christ's essence*, and in *Christ's essence*, the Word of Christ became man. The soul's desire, or *creative command* <note>original: *Fiat*</note>, receives or impresses this into its own holy *essence* which had disappeared in *Adam*. Here, *Adam* rises in *Christ* and becomes *Christ* (the second *Adam* or the Anointed One) according to the heavenly *essence* and divine Word; and from this *essence* of *Christ*, divine knowledge proceeds out of the Word of God.
   53. Thus, the children of God are *the temple of the Holy Spirit which dwells in them*, and so they speak God's Word. Without this, there is no true knowing or willing, but merely fables and *Babel*—a confusion created by the crafty serpent.
   54. Therefore, Christ called the *Pharisees a "seed of serpents" and a "generation of vipers."* Although they were the High Priests, He knew them to be vipers in their very essence, for they had formed their will in the *serpent’s essence*. They carried the words of *Moses* in their mouth, but they mixed the *serpent’s essence* into them, just as many still do today. In such cases, the Devil in the flesh carries God's Word on his tongue yet only uses it to hide the *serpent’s essence*, introducing a *diabolical essence* into the literal word. From this, *Babel*, the mother of all *spiritual unfaithfulness* <note>original: *whoredome*</note>, is born—a mere verbal contention and wrangling over words, where the *essence* of the Devil and the serpent opposes the divine *essence* within the formed Divine Word.
   55. But it must be this way, so that the formed and conceived Word in God's children may be stirred up, sharpened, and exercised, and the truth may come to light. Dear brethren, this is the *inheritance* which we have received from *Adam and Eve*, and that is the reason the body must die.

...whoever is angry with his brother is guilty of judgment. For that anger is a conception within the *serpent’s nature* <note>original: "Serpents Ens"; in this context, "Ens" refers to the corrupted spiritual substance or essence of humanity after the Fall</note>, which must be cut off by the *judgment of God* from the *Good Being*. *And whosoever shall say to his brother Racha, shall be in danger of the Council* <note>Racha: an Aramaic term of contempt meaning "empty-headed" or "worthless"</note>. For the desire for <margin> * Or revenge </margin> revenge arises in the center of the dark, fiery wheel of *eternal nature*. Therefore, in the *fire-soul*, there is a form of the *fire-word* [acting] like a wheel, similar to madness. The soul's fiery form stands in this "Racha" as a mad, furious wheel that confuses the *essence* in the *body* and destroys or shatters the understanding into pieces. For every "Racha" desires to destroy *God’s image*. Thus, the *soul* hangs on the wheel of *eternal nature*—that is, on the *center of the horrible, anxious birth*—as was mentioned before concerning the *center of the birth of nature*.

63. Moreover, Christ says: *Whoever says to his brother, "You fool," shall be in danger of hellfire.* This happens when the *conceived will* has formed itself in the furious wrath of *God’s anger* and introduced it into the *serpent’s nature*. It then stands in the furious wheel as if mad. If it now purposefully continues and forms that word, speaking it forth against its brother and igniting a hateful enmity in the *serpent’s nature* within him, the same word burns in his *expressed word* in the fire of *God’s anger*. He is guilty of it because he has ignited it in his "Racha."

64. Therefore, Christ said: *If you are going to offer your gift, go first and be reconciled to your offended brother or neighbor.* Otherwise, he brings his *wrath* into your offering and holds you back in your desire toward God, so that you cannot reach the *holy being* <note>original: "holy Ens"</note> which otherwise washes away the *turmoil* <note>original: "Turba"; a term used by the author to describe the spirit of wrath, disturbance, or destruction that disrupts the divine order</note> in your *ignited vanity*.

65. For the *word "fool"* is, in its very *essence*, nothing but an ignited, wrathful, fiery wheel—an outrageous madness. He who calls his neighbor that without cause has brought forth a word in the fire-wheel of *God’s wrath* and is guilty of it. For the word produced has arisen out of the *nature of the soul and body* <note>original: "Ens of the Soule and Body"</note>.

66. When every word is formed, it first awakens its own *nature* <note>original: "Ens"</note> from which it originates. Then it leads itself forth through the *counsel of the five senses* against its brother. Now, whoever uses such a wrathful, devouring fire-word against his brother sows into the *anger of God*. He is in danger *of reaping the fruit which he has sown when it springs up and grows*.

67. Therefore, take heed and beware, O Man, of what you think, speak, or desire to do! Look well always at what kind of zeal you stand in—whether it is divine or only of your own poisonous nature! You, father; you, mother; you, brother and sister, who proceed and come from one *blood* and one *nature* <note>original: "Ens"</note>, and mutually *assimilate* <note>original: "Assimulate"; to become similar or share the same substance</note> with each other like a tree with its branches: think and consider what kind of *sound* [or tune] you introduce into the vital *being* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of your fellow-twigs and branches. Is it *God’s love-word* or his *word of anger*? If you do not destroy the introduced evil again with *love*, and introduce the *love-essence* into the *anger* [to overcome and reconcile it], then that *substance* must come into <margin> * Or before </margin> the *judgment*.

# CHAPTER 23. Of Adam and His Eve. 111

...it only more open, and accused them as revolting, faithless rebels; for God’s anger did awake in them and arraigned them now before the severe judgment, to devour them into itself, as into the dark world, as happened to Lucifer.

<margin>The state, condition, or thing which caused the Earth to tremble, etc.</margin>

3. And this is the place where the Earth trembled at the death of Christ, and the rocks split apart: here God’s anger shut up the holy <term>Ens</term><note>Ens: A Latin term used by Boehme meaning "essence," "being," or "fundamental substance."</note> of the heavenly humanity in death; which Christ, when he destroyed death on the Cross, opened again, at which the wrath—in the curse of the earth and rocks—shook and trembled.

4. And here was the painful combat before God’s anger, in which combat Christ in the Garden (when he prayed and was to overcome this anger) sweated drops of blood, when he said: *"Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; but if it be not possible but that I must drink it, your will be done."*

5. Christ on the Cross had to drink down this wrathful anger, which was awakened in Adam’s essence, into his holy heavenly Ens, and change it with great love into divine joy. Of this, the drink of gall and vinegar—being a mixed drink which the Jews gave him—was a <term>type</term><note>original: "type"; a symbolic representation or foreshadowing.</note>, signifying what was done inwardly in the humanity of Christ.

6. For the outward image of man should also be redeemed from anger and death and arise again out of the Earth: therefore Christ’s outward humanity from the kingdom of this world must also drink of this cup, which God the Father had filled for Adam in his anger. Christ had to drink the same, and change the anger into love; therefore Christ said: *"Is it possible? Then let it pass from me."* But it was not possible to overcome the anger unless the sweet name Jesus drank it into itself and changed it into joy. Then Christ said: *"Father! Your will be done, and not the will of my humanity."*

7. God’s will should also have been fulfilled in Adam, but he exalted his own will by the serpent’s craft. Now the humanity of Christ upon the Cross must give *this own self-will* unto the anger to be devoured; but the holy name Jesus brought it into the death of selfhood, so that it must die in the wrathful death and enter again through death in his Resurrection into the true resignation—namely, into the divine harmony.

8. Adam, when he had awakened the anger in him, stood in Paradise in great shame and scorn before God and all holy angels, and the devils mocked and derided him: that this image of God, which should possess his royal throne, had become a monstrous beast. And into this scorn Christ had to enter, and suffer himself to be reviled, mocked, spit upon, whipped, and crowned with thorns as a false king; for Adam was a king and <term>Hierarch</term><note>Hierarch: A chief ruler or a leader of sacred things.</note>, but had become false and rebellious.

9. Here Christ stood in his stead and was condemned to death; for Adam also should have been judged by God’s anger. Here Adam—that is, Christ in Adam’s humanity—stood in his stead. Adam should have been rejected as a curse, even as a scorn before Heaven and Earth; and in sum, the whole process of Christ, from his Incarnation unto his Ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, is Adam’s estate—what Adam had merited as a <term>malefactor</term><note>malefactor: a criminal or wrongdoer.</note>, Christ himself had to take upon him.

# 112 Of Adam and his Eve.
## CHAPTER 23

...redeem him in Adam's person, and bring the life out of death once again.

10. Adam was made by the word of God, but he fell from God's Love-word into His Anger-word. Thus God, out of mere grace, did again awaken His Love-word in the deepest humility. Love and mercy [manifested] in Adam’s wrathful image, and He introduced the great Love-<term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the essential nature or being of a thing</note> into the fire of the awakened anger, and changed the angry Adam, through Christ, into a holy **ONE**.

11. Moses describes it very clearly, but a veil lies before the <margin>Verse 8.</margin> bestial man so that he does not recognize Him; for he says: *And they heard the voice of the Lord God, which walked in the Garden when the day grew cool, and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God among the trees.*

12. Moses says they heard the voice of the Lord God, which walked in the garden. What is this "voice" which was [or stirred] in the garden? For Adam's ears were dead to divine hearing and were instead awakened in wrath. He could no longer, by his own power, hear God’s holy voice, for he was dead to the Kingdom of Heaven and to divine holiness—just as God had told him: *In the day that you eat of this tree, you shall die.*

13. The voice was God's anger, which forced its way into Adam’s essence when the day became cool. Understand that the eternal day in Adam’s essence was awakened in cold and heat; therefore, they now heard the voice of God the Lord in His anger within their own essence. For the <term>Turba</term> <note>original: "Turba"; Jacob Boehme’s term for the "spirit of turmoil" or the destructive power of divine wrath awakened by sin</note> was awakened; the Tone or Hearing of the dark world did sound [or ring its sad knell].

14. But that which walked in the garden and called Adam back was another voice, which broke forth out of the anger and walked [or moved] in the garden. For the phrase "He who walked in the garden" <note>original German: "Der gieng im Garten"</note> is the point of difference or note of distinction; it signifies the voice of **JESUS** proceeding <margin>Jehovah <note>original Hebrew: יְהוָֹה</note></margin> <margin>Tetragrammaton <note>original Greek: Τετραγράμματον</note></margin> <margin>The Name of Four Letters <note>original Latin: Nomen Quatuor Literarum</note></margin> <margin>That Name of four Letters.</margin> from **JEHOVAH**. The voice was the **TETRAGRAMMATON** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, but that which walked in the garden was the **TONE** (the sound), namely, the center of the light-world. The voice of the **TETRAGRAMMATON** is the center of the fire-world (the First Principle), and the **TONE** is the Second Principle. Just as fire and light are one, but separate themselves into a twofold source when they manifest, the same is to be considered here.

15. The voice of the fire-world entered into the essence of Adam and Eve, and they heard it; therefore they were afraid and crept among the trees. But the voice of the light-world is this of which <margin>* Text, "He" [or "The"]</margin> Moses spoke: "He who walked in the garden" <note>original German: "Der gieng im Garten"</note>. The holy voice walked in the garden of Paradise, for the word "He" <note>original German: "Der"</note> denotes the person of Christ, who walked in the Spirit in the garden. He went forth from the fire's center, took possession of Paradise, and intended to invest Adam with it again.

16. Therefore Moses now says: *And the Lord God called to Adam, and <margin>Verse 9.</margin> said to him, "Where are you?"* Why did He not say, "Adam and Eve, where are you?" No, He called to Adam—namely, to the first image which He created in Paradise, and not to the "man and woman" [as separate fallen entities]. For He who called was He who walked in the garden: the word of the light-world, the voice of the Second Principle, which called them back.

Within this, the holy angelic life exists and bears the name of the great holy God, namely the holy word of the Deity.

Thus, we understand very clearly how God, out of great love, promised the *Serpent-bruiser* <note>A traditional title for Christ, based on the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would bruise the head of the serpent</note> to fallen man, and espoused and betrothed it to the virgin-like and disappeared center, giving Himself as a help and companion. For when they had fallen from God and made themselves monstrous, the image made from the clay <note>original: "limus"</note> of the earth became wholly animalistic. It lived in opposition, in imbalance, in sickness, and also in heat and cold, just like all other beasts.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;52. Now, therefore, God told them what their labor, work, and employment should be in this world: *namely, that they should bring forth children in sorrow with painful smart, in trouble and distress, and eat the herb of the field*. They must now clothe their bestial image in turmoil and burdensome care, in toil and labor, until the man of the four elements—in the bestial serpent's image—should again be broken and dissolved, returning to the earth from which he was taken and extracted as clay <note>original: "limus"</note>.

**Chapter 25. And placing the Cherub before the garden.** **127**

16. When Reason hears one speak of *Paradise*, then it understands only a certain place *apart*; and it is even so: there was a certain place which was called *the Garden in Eden* where *Adam* and *Eve* were tempted, and from which place they were driven after the fall. But yet, the whole world was such a *Paradise* before the Curse. However, since God knew the fall would happen, the holy *Paradise* was only opened unto them in *one certain place*; for to what end should the whole world bring forth Paradisiacal fruit, seeing there was no creature upon the Earth that was capable of enjoying it?

17. But *Adam* and *Eve* were nevertheless brought into *Paradise*, so that, although this first body should fall and come to ruin, they and their children might, by the new *regeneration* in the Spirit of Christ, enter in again through this fire-sword. This mystery is exceedingly great.

18. For Prince *Lucifer*, before the time of the Created Earth, sat in the heavenly essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> in the Angelic world in the place of *this world*, wherein the essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the Earth was comprehended in the creative word <note>original: "Fiat"; literally "let it be done"</note> and brought into a solid state <note>original: "Compaction"</note>. His false imagination had tainted the <margin>t. Made it subject to infection and pollution.</margin> clay <note>original: "limus"</note> before it was solidified; it was the place of his hierarchies. Now, the outward body of man was taken out of the clay <note>original: "limus"</note> of the Earth in the *Creative Word* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"</note> and formed according to the property of the human life, which was in the *Word*. The word formed (by or through the creative word <note>original: "Fiat"</note>) the essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> or clay <note>original: "limus"</note> of the Earth according to the form of the human soul-like life which was in the word. And since God had set himself, through his word, to be judge against the false *infection* and desire of the Devil—to judge him and his kindled wickedness which he had brought into substance—the <margin>u. Or Sword of execution.</margin> judicial sword was already in the clay <note>original: "limus"</note> of the Earth from which *Adam* was made.

19. For when God created the Earth, he <margin>x. Certainly appointed and set a time.</margin> established its time, when he would *keep* the judgment and sever the evil from the good, and give the *evil* as a habitation to the apostate prince. But because the Good in the hidden <note>original: "occluſe"; enclosed or shut away</note> Earth was without heavenly creatures (since its Prince was cast out), God created *Adam* as another ruler <note>original: "Hierarch"</note> out of this good essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> to be a *ruler* of this place; and from this came the Devil's *envy* against man and all good creatures of this world.

20. But now we are here to consider the *apostasy* <note>original: "Apoſtacy"; the rebellion or falling away</note> of man, with the *sword of the Cherub*; for Saint *Paul* says: *we are chosen in Christ Jesus before the foundation of the world was laid*. But when the branch or sprout is to be born and receive its beginning in the *essence* of the root, the *essence* then forms itself into such a twig as the root is perceived at that time in its power and free will, by both the superior and inferior *constellation* <note>referring to both astrological influences and spiritual alignments acting upon the plant</note>.

32. The same is also to be understood in man: as the will is in the *seed*—that is, as the desire of the father and mother, together with other influences from the stars and elements, and even sometimes from the Devil’s assaults and insinuations at that time—even *such a spirit* is formed in the *essence* of the seed. Sometimes it is an angel, if the parents are in *holy desire* [or in the true faith of the engrafted Word]; sometimes also it is a beast, a serpent, and an image of the Devil, both according to the *essence* of the *soul* and the *outward flesh*.

33. The power of the manifested Word gives itself into *all things*, into everything according to its will, according to the desire in the *essence*. For the desire in the *essence* is what forms the *Word*, namely, the sound of life. As it is written: *as the people are, so is the God they have; with the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* <note>referencing Psalm 18:25-26; the idea that God manifests to people according to their own spiritual state</note>. This is to be understood entirely concerning the *Expressed Word* in the *Fiat*, namely, in the *desire of nature*. And therefore, God has espoused and betrothed *another word* out of the center of His love to the image of man, so that, although he has arisen out of an evil property, yet the free will <margin>Note:</margin> has *power* and instruction to disclaim its *selfhood* <note>original: "Selfehood"; the ego-driven state of being separated from God</note> and die to itself in this holy, incorporated Word. And then the *Fiat* begets and forms another *new* creature in the *free will out of the essence.*

34. The *possibility* lies *in all men*, but the making or forming of the child of God belongs now to the holy *Fiat* in the newly introduced Word. For it lies *not on any man's self-willing, contriving, running, and toiling,* but on *God’s mercy* <note>referencing Romans 9:16</note>. <margin>Note.</margin> He has *mercy upon whom he pleases* <note>referencing Romans 9:18</note>, namely, only upon those who, with their free will, die to their selfhood.

# CHAPTER 27. Of Cain's and Abel's Offering. Genesis 4. 143

6. Just as the free will of the inward world has conceived itself in the *outward world* and works through it, so too the soul's free will—which also has its origin out of the abyss—incorporates <note>original: "immasseth," meaning to take on mass or substance</note> itself into *something* so that it might be manifested, and thereby be able to move and act in God’s sight.

7. Since *Adam’s body* was made from the *clay* <note>original: "limus"</note> of the earth and also from the *clay* of the holy heaven—which heavenly *clay* in *Adam* had now disappeared—the free will had the power to incorporate <note>or conceive</note> itself into a *holy form* and act, work, pray, and supplicate before God. Therefore, they made *burnt offerings* of the fruits of the earth; *Cain* brought fruit from the ground, and <margin>Genesis 4:3–4</margin> *Abel* also brought the *firstlings of his flock*, and they ignited these with fire.

8. But you must understand this as a *magical fire* (like that of *Moses*), for *Moses* declares it so as well: God looked graciously upon the offering of *Abel* and *not upon Cain's*. This means they brought offerings before God, and the free will of the soul was meant to press earnestly into God with its *prayer*. Therefore, it required a <gloss>subject or means</gloss> *substance* when it departed from the human house of corruption toward God, so that it might work within *something*. Therefore, the imagination of the will incorporated <note>or imagined</note> itself through the offering, and God ignited *Abel's* offering with the *holy fire* in the goal <note>original: "Aym"</note> of the Covenant, which in the fullness of time would *again* ignite itself in *the soul's fire*.

9. In this, the will of *Abel's* soul <gloss>fashioned or formed an idea</gloss> of itself into a *holy substance* and pressed—with the desire of the formed free soul's will—before and into God's free will. The will of the Devil and the Serpent could not endure this; even the will of the Serpent and Devil within *Cain* understood well that the goal of the Covenant opened itself in the *Holy Fire* through *Abel's desire* and *prayer*.

10. Therefore, he wanted to kill *Abel’s body* according to his earthly *clay* <note>original: "limus"</note>, lest such *children* should be fathered by him and he might lose his kingdom within man. But God would *not* ignite the offering of *Cain*. Now, *Moses* places a veil over this and says that God <gloss>would not have respect to</gloss> *look graciously upon Cain's offering*.

11. The igniting of the *external offering* was a symbol of the *internal Spirit*. For the soul's spirit in the free will (as the center of light) was ignited with God’s love-fire, and the *imagination* of the body also (meaning the heavenly part) was ignited in the offering with the *fire of the holy part of the Earth*—which lies *hidden* within the Curse. Therein, the free will of the soul and the free will in the *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the heavenly part of the body incorporated itself into a *substance*, and with that, it pressed into the presence of God’s *holiness*.

It would introduce a heavenly, *holy essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> into the disappeared *essence* of the heavenly part and quicken it to life again in the *revealed power of Jesus*.

# CHAPTER XXIX.

*Shows how the Adamic Tree has put forth and opened itself out of its trunk, and introduced itself into boughs, branches, twigs, and fruit; out of which sprouting or manifestation the invention of all arts and <margin>Or Polities (political systems)</margin> governments has arisen.*

*The Deep Gates out of the Center of the Eternal and also the Temporal Nature, showing how the Eternal Wisdom has introduced itself into a formal [visible and ideal] contemplation.*

<margin>Genesis chapter 4</margin> 1. THE eternal divine understanding is a free-will, not arisen either from anything or by anything; it is its own peculiar seat and dwells only and alone in itself, unperceived by anything. For beyond and without it is nothing, and that same NOTHING is only ONE, and yet it is also as a nothing to itself. It is the only will of the <term>Abyss</term><note>original: "Abysse"; in the context of Boehme's philosophy, this is the "Ungrund," the groundless void or nothingness from which God emerges</note>, and it is neither near nor far off, neither high nor low; but it is ALL, and yet as a nothing; for it is in itself no contemplation, sensation, or perception by which it might find a likeness in itself.

For this reason, Abel and all his descendants <margin>or successors</margin> became martyrs.

Therefore, the Divine Word re-established itself <margin>espoused, betrothed, or promised itself</margin> within her as a center of regeneration.

The fruit that Christ would bring forth was to generate the human tree anew, not to produce other twigs from his own loins. And therefore Abel...

The meaning is this: whoever kills the life—that is, whatever free will murders its own life—vengeance shall be taken on it eternally in the *seven properties of the dark world.*

59. And in this place, we are to consider the great mysteries further. The *seven properties of the human tree*, which produce and manifest the life of the *wonders of God*, had now spread themselves as far as *Lamech*. The dominion of the world was now fully brought forth in nature with *Lamech*; for *Lamech* was the *seventh* man in the root of the wonders arising from the first stock. 61. And he also looked forward and saw how things would turn out in these *wonders of the world*. He saw how his children would lead the life they received from him by propagation into a *Babylon* of folly and corrupt it. Because of this, he looked especially upon the Word from which human life had sprung, and how life in the *spirit of the wonders* of the world would introduce itself into a seventy-seven-fold word of languages and nations, as happened at *Babel*. He saw how the free will of nature would go astray from the *only God* and become corrupt, and that it would be avenged seventy-seven-fold. That is, every tongue and speech would be avenged in the *anger of God*. This was because they would corrupt *Lamech's* life, which they received from him by birth; and the *wrath of God* would avenge this in the free will of his children, divided into various languages.

62. For the *spirit* saw ahead how the free will would give itself up and devote itself to *self-interest*, turning away from the *only God*. It saw how the *anger of God* would seize upon and confound the *natural spirit of the wonders* in man—namely, the *soul of the outward world*. From this would arise the *great Babylon of conflict* regarding *God’s being and will*; and the *spirit* said this should be avenged seventy-seven-fold in *Lamech*.

Previously, understanding lay in one *sound* [voice or harmony], but now the *Racha* entered it, confounding and shattering it into *seventy-seven parts*.

**CHAPTER XXX.**
**Of the Line of the Covenant.**

1. The Line of the *Covenant* is not to be understood as if the Covenant fell *only* upon this line; no, the Covenant <margin>Passes upon, belongs to, or is bestowed upon.</margin> falls only upon the *Life* which was in the Word before the times of humanity. The line of *Seth* passes only upon the manifestation in the flesh, in which line the Word in the Covenant would externally manifest itself in the flesh. But the Spirit proceeding from the Center in the Covenant falls *as well upon Cain’s line as upon Abel’s*; yet in *Cain’s* line it falls in the *spirit*, and in *Seth’s* in the *external mouth* [or manifestation]—that is, in the office and ministry of teaching and preaching. For *Seth* sprang forth according to the Spirit, out of the Covenant, where the Spirit moved itself in the incorporated Word in the Covenant; and *Cain* was comprehended under the spirit of nature.

2. For by *Cain’s* line the arts were brought forth to light, which were a *wonder of the Divine wisdom*, contemplation, and formation—namely, of the *Formed Word* through and in *nature*. And in *Seth*, the Word was brought into a formal life—that is, into a *spiritual contemplation*—wherein the Word of God beheld itself with wisdom in a spiritual <margin>Form or figure.</margin> *image*. In *Cain’s* line, it beheld itself in a naturally formed word; and *both* serve to set forth the wonderful deeds of God.

3. It is not as *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; the author uses this name for the "confused" or corrupt institutional church</note> judges: that God, out of His own purpose and fixed counsel, has *thus predestined and chosen* one part of humanity in His anger for condemnation, and the other part for life. Those who judge this way are still under the number *seventy and seven* <note>original: "Seventy and Seven"; a reference to the multiplication of vengeance in Genesis 4:24, here signifying spiritual confusion</note> in the multiplication of the Word. For the Promise was given to *Adam* before *Cain* was conceived; the Covenant regarding *grace* rested in *Adam and Eve*. But the Spirit of Sanctification and Regeneration by *Christ* passed only upon *the seed of the woman*—namely, upon the Seed of the Kingdom of Heaven which was shut up. That is, it passed upon the light's *tincture* <term>tincture: in Böhme’s writing, this refers to a spiritual essence or transformative power</term>, upon the *Matrix of Venus* <note>original: "Matrix of Venus"; a mystical term representing the generative principle of divine love and light</note>, in which *Adam* (when he was both man and woman) should have propagated himself in pure desire and love. Since this could not happen [due to *Adam’s* strong earthly imagination], that part was taken from *Adam* and made into a woman.

4. But when the woman became earthly, the heavenly part of this matrix [which was for the production] of the heavenly birth was shut up in death. Into this *matrix*, the Word of God again incorporated itself with the Covenant, to open and manifest himself in this matrix with a living and heavenly *seed*, and to destroy the *power of death*.

5. For the Word would not open itself in the formed word of nature,

11. ...the Name of the Lord. For the name **Enos** signifies, in the Language of Nature, a Divine Pleasure <term>original: "Lubet," a term used by Boehme to describe a divine longing, inclination, or the first movement of the will toward expression</term> through the life, wherein the Formed Word would behold itself in the sound and voice of life. Therefore, the Spirit of God began to teach out of the Covenant through the life of man, concerning God and His being and will. This was the beginning of divine contemplation through the "formed Wisdom" in the Word, where the Word beheld itself through the wisdom of the formed human voice.

12. And as life formed itself through Cain’s line through the wonders of the "formed wisdom" in Nature—with all kinds of arts, works, dominions, governments, and orders, and introduced them all to display God's wondrous deeds and acts (namely, for a contemplation of evil and good, light and darkness)—so likewise, the Spirit of God brought forth from the Line of the Covenant in the manifested Word the wonders of divine holiness, truth, righteousness, love, and patience. By the preaching of the formed Word, the Spirit declared what the holy and spiritual Kingdom of God is.

13. In Cain, the kingdom of nature was represented, and in Abel and Seth, the supernatural divine Kingdom. Both of these arose together and proceeded within one another as a demonstration <note>original: "Remonstrance"</note> or contemplation of the Divine Pleasure in the formed wisdom; and each put itself forward in a special way into its own visible field as a wonder.

14. For from Adam even until Lamech in the line of wonders <note>the lineage of Cain</note>, there are seven generations; and in the other line—namely, in the Line of the Covenant from Adam until Enoch—there are also seven generations. **Enoch** is the eighth, signifying a beginning of the prophetic spirit; for in the first seven generations, the form of the spiritual Kingdom proceeding from the Tree of Life was established.

15. Adam was the source <note>original: "stock"</note>, for his life takes its origin out of the Word. But since the life of nature in him predominated over the life in the formed Word—seeking supreme dominion and obscuring the life proceeding from the Word—the Word itself freely gave itself with a Covenant to be a Life within him. The Word set forth its figure in Abel, showing how the natural life should and must be broken, so that the Word of divine power might again spring forth afresh out of the first life.

16. Thus, Abel was the figure of the Second Adam, Christ; and therefore, he had to be slain for the sake of the Covenant. For Christ was to kill the exalted, haughty natural will and bring forth a new one. Therefore, Abel also was not to beget any natural child; otherwise, it would have been foreign to nature, for all should proceed from one source. The Word would spring forth anew through the only Tree in the Covenant, so that the children of Grace might be brought forth out of the Tree of Nature, just as the dew arises out of the <margin>Or, Morning-break</margin> daybreak <note>Boehme frequently uses "daybreak" or "aurora" to describe the dawning of divine light within the soul</note>.

17. For in this way, the figure of the new birth was represented from the stem: namely, the line went forth out of Adam, who was the first; Abel the second; Seth the third; and Enos the fourth, where men began to teach of the spiritual Kingdom. <margin>Or, Cainan</margin> **Kenan** was the fifth, which signifies in the language of nature a <margin>Re-apprehended</margin> forth-going, re-conceived pleasure <note>original: "Lubet"</note> or desire of divine contemplation, in which the taught Word formed itself—namely, in prayer, in the desire of the will, and also in their offerings.

By these numbers and names, the Spirit points in each line especially to seven of the forth-proceeding properties of the Tree and powers of the wonders, indicating how the powers of the wonders should afterward organize themselves into governments, how one figure should arise out of the other, and how one should destroy and break down the other, setting forth another form out of the destruction, as has been brought to pass in the *spiritual* <margin>Ecclesiastical and temporal.</margin> and worldly governments. Therefore, observe and mark this with precise exactness.

## CHAPTER 31.
***Of Enoch's Wonderful Line.***

Moses writes: *Enoch fathered <note>original: "begat"</note> Methuselah* <margin>Genesis 5:21</margin>. In the language of nature, this name signifies as much as a *forth-proceeding voice* <margin>Or, Out-going</margin>, which indicates and denotes the *spirit of Enoch*. This voice *forms* <margin>Frame or comprehend</margin> itself into a body—namely, into *nature*—and goes forth in strong might through the word. When the conceived or formed word has proceeded forth, it then contemplates itself; for the *syllable (-SA-)* is a fiery glimpse of light, and the *syllable (-LAH-)* is the forth-proceeded word, which perceives the property and kind of *Ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical term for "being" or "essence."</term> it is, in which the word has formed (or contained) itself. The *Divine Sound* beholds itself in the human *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> and *word*, contemplating how the free will proceeding from the human essence has introduced the Divine voice or *breath* into a form of the Spirit.

# CHAP. XXXII.
## *Of the Covenant between God and Noah.*

*Gen. 6:18.* 1. God said to Noah, "*I will establish a Covenant with you, and you shall go into the Ark with your sons, and your sons' wives with you.*" We have a great, significant, and remarkable *example* here in *Noah* and his children. The Covenant was made with *Noah*, for his spirit was a revelation or a beaming forth of the formed Word within him, in the beginning and end of time. This beginning and end was the *Eternal Word*, which had committed itself to the *Covenant* <note>original: "espoused itself," meaning to marry or unite with</note>. In this Covenant, the soul of *Noah*—namely, the formed word of Eternal Nature—found *Grace* and obtained the confirmation of the Covenant of Grace.

2. As his *name* properly and uniquely signifies in the "language of nature" <note>This refers to the idea that names originally reflected the true essence of things</note>, it means "a beholding of the beginning and end." In this same beginning and end—specifically, in the Eternal *speaking* Word of the Father, which intended to manifest and reveal itself again in human life—*grace* was revealed and presented to *Noah*, so that God established and confirmed the Covenant with him.

3. And here we have a very excellent and emphatic example, which is exceedingly worth mentioning, in the *three sons of Noah*. In their characteristics, they sprang from the lineage of *Adam* in a threefold *line*. For we see that three nations (several sorts of people) arose from them, and that God included all *three* of them, with their *wives*, in the *Covenant of Grace* and commanded them also to go into the Ark—into the second monarchy <note>The "Second Monarchy" refers to the post-flood world or the second age of human history</note>—and did *not* exclude the worldly *Ham*.

4. First, it is highly important to consider that a *gate of grace* stands open to *all* people, and that God has *not* set any election or predestination *within nature*. Instead, the "election" or choice arises out of *free will* when it *turns* itself from good to evil.

5. Secondly, it is a *type* <note>a symbolic representation or foreshadowing</note> of the Three Principles. Namely, *Shem* is a type of the spiritual light-world in the Covenant; *Japheth* represents the fire-world, which was to be a guest in the light-world and a *mirror* of the great joy in the light-world; and *Ham* is a figure of the *Limus* <note>original: "Limus," a term often used in mystical theology to refer to the "slime" or "vital clay" of the earth from which Adam was created</note> of the earth, to which the curse and the *anger* of God cling. God took all three of these into the Covenant with *Noah* and brought them into the *Ark*.

6. For every person has these three worlds upon them and *within* them; and the Covenant in the Word was given so that the *whole* person should be redeemed.

7. For *Japheth* signifies the "fire-soul"; *Shem* represents the image of God from the light-world—that is, the spirit from the Holy Word; and *Ham* signifies the *Limus* of the earth along with the outward dominion or region of the air and the magical, ethereal constellations <note>Referring to the astrological and physical influences on the human body</note>, together with the body, which shall be *freed* from the *curse* by the Covenant and arise

It emphasizes that grace is available to all humanity, regardless of lineage, and argues against natural predestination.</summary>

59. In an office, you must either serve God or the Devil, for you cannot serve two masters alike; for "self" and "resignation" are two distinct things. This officer is in the ministry and service of the evil Adam, in whom the Devil has his throne, and helps him to pronounce the sentence of justice.

60. Oh, you worldly judge, do not rely upon the Tower of Babel, upon worldly determinations, ordinances, and conclusions, or upon human institutions, statutes, laws, and decrees: the top thereof reaches not into heaven. That is only the height of the confusion of strife and a <margin>* Or, mistake.</margin> * misunderstanding. God sees you in your very heart; He proves and tries your will and desire. The law does not plead for you before God, even though you conduct yourself according to it, when your heart knows it ought to be quite otherwise. Think no other way with yourself, but that you pronounce the sentence of justice for the Devil and serve him under a hypocritical mantle or cloak. Justice and right are God's, and are God Himself; but <margin>† Or, unrighteousness.</margin> † wrong is the Devil's, and is the Devil himself. That master whom you serve is he who will reward you and pay you your wages—he himself will be your wages; and this you are to expect in your office.

This may also be understood by the diligent consideration of astronomy according to astrology, wherein the natural effect and working is prefigured.

36. [The hunger of pride] takes others' sweat and the flesh from their bones and devours it, yet has nothing; instead, it always lies like poison sucking itself out. The more greedy covetousness is to devour, the greater is its son, *Envy*. It desires to possess everything alone for itself, yet it has *no place of rest* in heaven, this world, or hell. It can remain neither in heaven nor in hell; it stands only in the hunger of covetousness and is the *life* of covetousness.

38. The fourth property of hunger, covered under Christ’s mantle, is *Anger*, which is the son of Envy, and Covetousness is its grandfather. What Envy cannot *sting* to death, Anger will strike and *fell* <note>original: "fell" — meaning to knock down or cut down, like a tree.</note> to death. It is so evil and wicked that it breaks and shatters bones to pieces. It always *thirsts* for murder, solely so that its father and grandfather—namely, covetousness, envy, and pride—may have room enough. It destroys body and soul in their own kind of *fatness* and wastes country and city; it is so wicked that it would destroy heaven and hell, and yet it has no rest anywhere.

They are so very hungry that hell dwells *in their four elements*, and the kingdom of the devil *stands in their figure*. <margin>* Consists of that which their pasture, condition, or quality represents and expresses.</margin>

**Genesis XLII.** This forty-second chapter of *Genesis*, concerning *Joseph* and his brothers, is a symbolic figure. It shows how a converted Christian—who has already entered into Christ's "process" <note>The author uses the term "process" to describe the spiritual journey or path of transformation modeled on the life and suffering of Christ.</note> and has now overcome—ultimately forgives and rewards his enemies with generosity. These were the enemies who brought him into Christ’s process through their persecution, wicked schemes, and advice. It also shows how their *sins* are set before them and how they are brought into anxiety and need. Finally, it demonstrates how they are released from pain and punishment by sheer grace, and how God is so gracious to them upon their conversion that He not only removes the punishment but also blesses them with His gifts and benefits, just as *Joseph* did for his brothers here.

2. Next, this figure also represents how earnestly and severely God stands against sin, just as *Joseph* did against his brothers. Yet God is not eager to punish the repenting sinner with the harshest severity. Instead, He sets Himself strictly against the soul in its conscience so that sin may be awakened and acknowledged. This allows repentance to grow greater, so that a person in such terror may be humbled for sin, abandon it completely, be angry with it, and utterly hate it—knowing that sin carries such a terrible judgment *within it*.

4. Moses’ words follow thus: <margin>Genesis 43:1, 2, 3, 4, 5.</margin> *“The famine was severe in the land, and when the corn was spent which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them: ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’ Then Judah answered and said: ‘The man strictly ordered and charged us, saying: You shall not see my face unless your brother be with you. **This symbolic representation is as follows:**

5. The soul of man exists within **Three Principles**; <note>Boehme’s "Three Principles" are: 1) The dark fire-world (the Father’s property), 2) The light love-world (the Son’s property), and 3) The physical, outward world (the Spirit of the World).</note> namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, in the **Eternal Fire’s Nature**, and in the **Eternal Light’s Nature**—that is, in the **Love-fire**, which was extinguished in Adam, which is the cause of the current **strife**. And thirdly, it exists in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>, in the kingdom of this world—namely, in **mortality** and **restoration**.

6. Therefore, understand us correctly in this way: when the inward soul-ground—namely, the **eternal soul** from the Father’s property of the Word of God—turns back again and looks about for its **Little Pearl**, <note>Boehme often uses "the Pearl" to represent the lost spark of divine light or the image of God within the soul.</note> specifically for the property of the second principle of the angelic world, it will perceive that this was lost in Adam. From this realization arises its misery and its return. As soon as it returns again, God gives His **grace** into it once more, but it is unknown and **not understood by the soul**. And God <margin>God.</margin> desires that the inward fire-soul (the center of the eternal nature) should turn to God again through the voice of grace that was spoken or inspired into the soul in Paradise, which was once wholly part of its being.

7. In this **divine desire**, a great restlessness arises in the soul. It enters into repentance when it sees that it has lost its ability. It neither may, shall, nor can attain its first pearl again and reach divine **salvation** in any **other way** unless it turns with the power of its fire wholly back into the ground of this **indwelling grace** and gives itself up to it.

8. And now, when the outward **mortal** soul—the nature of the third principle of the kingdom of this world—sees this, it is afraid, just as Jacob was for his children. It always thinks it will lose body and life, goods and honor, and that its forms or faculties of life will be robbed of the outward power and authority which they have in this world.

9. Furthermore, the inward fiery soul **cannot** stir up its inward ground—the true **Benjamin**—and bring it along into **Egypt**, into the presence of **Joseph** (which signifies earnest repentance in the presence of **Jesus**), unless the **outward** soul from the spirit of the world is brought down, quite tamed and **subdued**, so that it also may in the end willingly **submit** to it. This allows the fiery **inward** great soul to move itself in all the Three Principles and stir up the most inward ground—namely, Joseph’s brother, the indwelling **Gate of Grace**—together with all the outward essences <note>In Boehme’s writing, "essences" refers to the active, living qualities or "being" of a soul's faculties.</note> of the outward soul, and bring them along into the work of repentance, into the presence of the true **Joseph** or **Jesus**.

10. For the fiery soul is threatened by Joseph (that is, by Jesus) that if—

13. It was difficult for him, and yet the famine and hunger pressed upon him so much that in the end he had to yield and be willing to let all his sons go into Egypt. His youngest son went along, and he was alone, like one who had no children. In the same way, the outward nature must completely leave behind whatever it has or is in itself—having no more power or ability regarding earthly things—and give up the selfhood of its inward soul (which stands in the "drawing" or attraction of God). This allows the inward soul to take the outward soul’s will along with it into conversion. Then the old Jacob—the old earthly Adamic body—remains alone in its house of sorrow, not knowing what will become of it. When its spirit must go along into conversion, then the **earthly Lucifer** within it—namely, the fleshy desire—thinks: "By this you will lose temporal honor and good things and be the fool of the world; this will not satisfy your goals and lusts."

It must pray for it and desire it from the true householder, Joseph or **JESUS**, and in such prayer and desire fall on its face in great humility before Joseph or Jesus and desire food from him.

15. The fact that Jacob’s sons had to go twice into Egypt for corn—and the first time they received enough corn yet still fell into danger and were kept as a pledge <margin>They were kept as a pawn or in custody.</margin>—has this inward meaning: when a person first turns to repentance, the terrible figure or aspect of his sins first stands before him. They rouse him up, and the conscience stands in the anger of God.

16. Just as the brothers of Joseph stood the first time before Joseph when he took them for spies, so also a person stands before God as a "spy" of divine grace. He thinks he will enter into repentance just this once so that his old sins may be forgiven him. However, he has not yet so strongly tamed his will that it intends to remain in such repentance all the days of its life while the body lasts. Instead, he thinks only of destroying sin in the conscience once and drowning the old sins in repentance and sorrow.
